## Build a Simple CRUD Go App with CockroachDB and the Go pgx Driver

[Use **pgx**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/build-a-go-app-with-cockroachdb)
[Use **GORM**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/build-a-go-app-with-cockroachdb-gorm)
[Use **lib/pq**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/build-a-go-app-with-cockroachdb-pq)
[Use **upper/db**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/build-a-go-app-with-cockroachdb-upperdb)

This tutorial shows you how build a simple CRUD Go application with CockroachDB and the [Go pgx driver](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx).

### Step 1. Start CockroachDB

Use CockroachDB Basic
Use a Local Cluster

#### Choose your installation method

You can install a CockroachDB Basic cluster using either the CockroachDB Cloud Console, a web-based graphical user interface (GUI) tool, or `ccloud`, a command-line interface (CLI) tool.

Use the Cloud Console (GUI)
**Use `ccloud` (CLI)**

#### Create a free cluster

Note:
Organizations without billing information on file can only create one CockroachDB Basic cluster.

1. If you haven't already, [sign up for a CockroachDB Cloud account](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/signup?referralId=docs_go_pgx).
1. [Log in](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/) to your CockroachDB Cloud account.
1. On the **Clusters** page, click **Create cluster**.
1. On the **Select a plan** page, select **Basic**.
1. On the **Cloud & Regions** page, select a cloud provider (GCP or AWS) in the **Cloud provider** section.
1. In the **Regions** section, select a region for the cluster. Refer to [CockroachDB Cloud Regions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/regions) for the regions where CockroachDB Basic clusters can be deployed. To create a multi-region cluster, click **Add region** and select additional regions.
1. Click **Next: Capacity**.
1. On the **Capacity** page, select **Start for free**. Click **Next: Finalize**.
1. On the **Finalize** page, click **Create cluster**.

Your cluster will be created in a few seconds and the **Create SQL user** dialog will display.

#### Create a SQL user

The **Create SQL user** dialog allows you to create a new SQL user and password.

1. Enter a username in the **SQL user** field or use the one provided by default.
1. Click **Generate & save password**.
1. Copy the generated password and save it in a secure location.
1. Click **Next**.

Currently, all new SQL users are created with admin privileges. For more information and to change the default settings, see [Manage SQL users on a cluster](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/managing-access#manage-sql-users-on-a-cluster).

#### Get the connection string

The **Connect to cluster** dialog shows information about how to connect to your cluster.

1. Select **General connection string** from the **Select option** dropdown.
1. Open the **General connection string** section, then copy the connection string provided and save it in a secure location.

The sample application used in this tutorial uses system CA certificates for server certificate verification, so you can skip the **Download CA Cert** instructions.

Note:
The connection string is pre-populated with your username, password, cluster name, and other details. Your password, in particular, will be provided *only once*. Save it in a secure place (Cockroach Labs recommends a password manager) to connect to your cluster in the future. If you forget your password, you can reset it by going to the **SQL Users** page for the cluster, found at `https://cockroachlabs.cloud/cluster/<CLUSTER ID>/users`.

Follow these steps to create a CockroachDB Basic cluster using the `ccloud` CLI tool.

Note:
The `ccloud` CLI tool is in Preview.

#### Install `ccloud`

Choose your OS:

**Mac**
**Linux**
**Windows**

You can install `ccloud` using either Homebrew or by downloading the binary.

#### Use Homebrew

1. [Install Homebrew](http://brew.sh/).
1. Install using the `ccloud` tap:

```
brew install cockroachdb/tap/ccloud

```

 $ pip3 install psycopg2

 Working with Programming Languages | 75


 2 Note that because of limitations in the psycopg2 driver, we need to replace the final “=” in the URL with “%3d.” Instead of cluster=grumpy-orca-56, we use cluster%3dgrumpy-orca-56.

 Building wheel for psycopg2 (setup.py) ... done Created wheel for psycopg2: filename=psycopg2-2.8.6-cp39-... Stored in directory: /Users/guyharrison/Li... Successfully built psycopg2 Installing collected packages: psycopg2 Successfully installed psycopg2-2.8.6

Now the following short program will connect to CockroachDB using a URL pro‐

vided on the command line and issue a SELECT statement:

 #!/usr/bin/env python3

 import psycopg2 import sys

 def main():

 if ((len(sys.argv)) !=2): sys.exit("Error:No URL provided on command line") uri=sys.argv[1]

 conn = psycopg2.connect(uri) with conn.cursor() as cur: cur.execute("""SELECT CONCAT('Hello from CockroachDB at ', CAST (NOW() as STRING))""") data=cur.fetchone() print ("%s" % data[0])

 main()

Here we connect to the CockroachDB Serverless database we established earlier in

the chapter:^2

 $ python helloCockroachDB.py \ 'postgres://guy:xxxxxx@free-tier6.gcp-asiasoutheast1.cockroachlabs.cloud:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=verifyfull&sslrootcert=/Users/guyharrison/CockroachDBCockroachDBKeys/ cc-ca.crt&options=--cluster%3dgrumpy-orca-56'

 Hello from CockroachDB at 2021-05-02 02:39:55.859734+00:00

And here we connect to a local CockroachDB cluster running in insecure mode:

 $ python helloCockroachDB.py 'postgres://root@localhost:26257?sslmode=disable' Hello from CockroachDB at 2021-05-02 02:33:00.755359+00:00

**76 | Chapter 3: Getting Started**


**Connecting to CockroachDB from Go**

The Go language is one of the fastest-growing programming languages, and it offers

high performance, modern programming paradigms, and a low footprint. Much of

the CockroachDB database platform is written in Go, so Go is a great choice for

CockroachDB development.

In this example, we’re going to use the pgx PostgreSQL driver for Go to connect to

the CockroachDB Serverless cluster we created earlier. First, we need to install the

driver:

 $ go env -w GO111MODULE=auto $ go get github.com/jackc/pgx

This short program connects to CockroachDB using the URL provided on the com‐

mand line, and issues a SELECT statement:

 package main

 import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/jackc/pgx" )

 func main() { uri := "postgresql://root@localhost:26257/bank?ssl=disabled" conn, err := pgx.Connect(context.Background(), uri) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Unable to connect to database: %v\n", err) os.Exit(1) } var text string err = conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), SELECT CONCAT('Hello from CockroachDB at ', CAST (NOW() as STRING))).Scan(&text) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "QueryRow failed: %v\n", err) os.Exit(1) }

 fmt.Println(text) }

 Working with Programming Languages | 77


Here, we connect to a CockroachDB Serverless cluster:

 $ go run helloCockroachDB.go \ "postgres://guy:xxxxxxx@free-tier6.gcp-asiasoutheast1.cockroachlabs.cloud:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=verifyfull&sslrootcert=$HOME/CockroachDBCockroachDBKeys/ cc-ca.crt&options=--cluster=grumpy-orca-56"

 Hello from CockroachDB at 2021-05-02 02:24:13.930662+00:00

And here we run the program to connect to a local CockroachDB cluster in insecure

mode:

 $ go run helloCockroach.go 'postgres://root@localhost:26257?sslmode=disable' Hello from CockroachDB at 2021-05-02 02:21:59.179171+00:00

1. [Log in](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/) to your CockroachDB Cloud account.
1. On the **Clusters** page, click **Create cluster**.
1. On the **Select a plan** page, select **Basic**.
1. On the **Cloud & Regions** page, select a cloud provider (GCP or AWS) in the **Cloud provider** section.
1. In the **Regions** section, select a region for the cluster. Refer to [CockroachDB Cloud Regions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/regions) for the regions where CockroachDB Basic clusters can be deployed. To create a multi-region cluster, click **Add region** and select additional regions.
1. Click **Next: Capacity**.
1. On the **Capacity** page, select **Start for free**. Click **Next: Finalize**.
1. On the **Finalize** page, click **Create cluster**.

Your cluster will be created in a few seconds and the **Create SQL user** dialog will display.

#### Create a SQL user

The **Create SQL user** dialog allows you to create a new SQL user and password.

1. Enter a username in the **SQL user** field or use the one provided by default.
1. Click **Generate & save password**.
1. Copy the generated password and save it in a secure location.
1. Click **Next**.

Currently, all new SQL users are created with admin privileges. For more information and to change the default settings, see [Manage SQL users on a cluster](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/managing-access#manage-sql-users-on-a-cluster).

#### Get the connection string

The **Connect to cluster** dialog shows information about how to connect to your cluster.

1. Select **General connection string** from the **Select option** dropdown.
1. Open the **General connection string** section, then copy the connection string provided and save it in a secure location.

The sample application used in this tutorial uses system CA certificates for server certificate verification, so you can skip the **Download CA Cert** instructions.

Note:
The connection string is pre-populated with your username, password, cluster name, and other details. Your password, in particular, will be provided *only once*. Save it in a secure place (Cockroach Labs recommends a password manager) to connect to your cluster in the future. If you forget your password, you can reset it by going to the **SQL Users** page for the cluster, found at `https://cockroachlabs.cloud/cluster/<CLUSTER ID>/users`.

Follow these steps to create a CockroachDB Basic cluster using the `ccloud` CLI tool.

Note:
The `ccloud` CLI tool is in Preview.

#### Install `ccloud`

Choose your OS:

**Mac**
**Linux**
**Windows**

You can install `ccloud` using either Homebrew or by downloading the binary.

#### Use Homebrew

1. [Install Homebrew](http://brew.sh/).
1. Install using the `ccloud` tap:

```
brew install cockroachdb/tap/ccloud

```

88: 
89: ## 1. Architecture: One Shared SQL Implementation (replaces v1 §1.1-1.4)
90: 
91: ### 1.1 Driver strategy — decision
92: 
93: **Question (per ChatGPT): "Why do PostgreSQL and CockroachDB need separate store implementations at all?"**
94: **Answer: they do not.** The §0.3 audit proves the SQL in `store/db/postgres/` is portable. The deltas are four:
95: 
96: 1. Connection string handling (DSN params, pool sizing) — `postgres.go:22-54`
97: 2. Transient-error detection + retry wrapper — `resilience.go`
98: 3. Transaction execution (8 manual `BeginTx` sites must become retry-capable on CRDB) — Section 4
99: 4. Migration execution mode — Section 5
100: 
101: **Design:** keep the single `store/db/postgres` package (it is the "PostgreSQL wire-protocol" implementation). Add a cockroach variant selected at runtime:
102: 
103: ```go
104: // store/db/postgres/postgres.go
105: func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
106:     return newDB(profile, false)
107: }
108: 
109: func NewCockroachDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
110:     return newDB(profile, true)
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: `DB` gains `isCockroach bool`, used only in: connection setup, `isTransientError`, and the `withTx` helper (Section 4). **No build tags** — the driver is selected at runtime via `MEMOS_DRIVER`, like the existing `postgres` case. This resolves C-1 completely: there is one implementation, one bug-fix path, one set of store methods. No `store/db/cockroach/` directory is created.
115: 
116: ### 1.2 Driver factory
117: 
118: `store/db/db.go`:
119: 
120: ```go
121: case "cockroach":
122:     driver, err = postgres.NewCockroachDB(profile)
123: ```
124: 
125: ### 1.3 Profile / DSN resolution
126: 
127: `internal/profile/profile.go` (per C-4):
128: 
129: ```go
130: if p.Driver == "cockroach" && p.DSN == "" {
131:     p.DSN = os.Getenv("COCKROACH_DSN")
132:     if p.DSN == "" {
133:         return errors.New("cockroach driver requires COCKROACH_DSN environment variable")
134:     }
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: - **No `DATABASE_URL` fallback** (C-4). A misconfigured `MEMOS_DRIVER=cockroach` with a Neon `DATABASE_URL` set must fail loudly at startup, never silently connect to Postgres.
139: - Reject `sslmode=disable` in `prod` mode at startup (defense in depth; H-2).
140: 
141: ### 1.4 Connection setup (cockroach variant)
142: 
143: ```go
144: dsn := profile.DSN
145: // Keep simple protocol: the migrator executes multi-statement SQL files (C-new-3),
146: // and CRDB documents prepared-statement staleness across schema changes.
147: if !strings.Contains(dsn, "default_query_exec_mode") {
148:     sep := "?"; if strings.Contains(dsn, "?") { sep = "&" }
149:     dsn += sep + "default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol"
150: }
151: db.SetMaxOpenConns(poolMaxOpenConns)   // COCKROACH_MAX_OPEN_CONNS, default 8
152: db.SetMaxIdleConns(poolMaxOpenConns / 2)
153: db.SetConnMaxLifetime(5 * time.Minute)
154: db.SetConnMaxIdleTime(1 * time.Minute)
155: ```
156: 
157: - **Pool sizing (H-1 + ChatGPT amendment):** read `COCKROACH_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` (default **8**, i.e., 4× the 2 vCPUs of a CRDB Cloud Basic cluster — `prod_checklist.md:351`). Do **not** derive from `runtime.NumCPU()` of the Fly machine (app host ≠ cluster).
158: - `sslmode=verify-full` with system CA is the CRDB Cloud default in the docs' connection strings; keep whatever `COCKROACH_DSN` specifies for local (`disable`) and require a non-`disable` mode in `prod`.
159: 
160: ### 1.5 Resilience (cockroach variant)
161: 
162: - `isTransientError`: add `"40001"` (serialization_retry) to the existing set (57P01/08006/08003/08001/08004).
163: - `isUniqueViolation`: unchanged — CRDB uses the same SQLSTATE `23505`.
164: - `RunResiliently`: unchanged behavior; note that statement-level retry is only applied to idempotent single statements (existing call sites); 40001 handling happens at transaction level via `withTx` (Section 4).
165: - **Never wrap migration code in retry** (C-new-5).
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 2. Schema Migration for CockroachDB
170: 
171: ### 2.1 Migration directory
172: 
173: Create `store/migration/cockroach/` containing:
174: 
175: | File | Purpose |
176: |------|---------|
177: | `LATEST.sql` | Full schema, adapted per Section 2.2 (copy of postgres LATEST.sql with PK/ID changes only) |
178: | `0.35/1__init.sql` | Marker file so `GetCurrentSchemaVersion()` finds versioned dirs (C-new-2); a no-op comment statement |
179: 
180: **Rationale (C-new-2):** the migrator requires `migration/{driver}/*/*.sql` glob matches. Fresh CRDB clusters boot via `preMigrate()` → `LATEST.sql` → `migration_history`; incremental files are only applied when a history entry older than the FS max exists. The marker dir must be kept at the current schema version (0.35 at time of writing) and bumped together with the code version.
181: 
182: **Incremental migration policy (C-3):**
183: 1. Every future migration lands in BOTH `store/migration/postgres/` and `store/migration/cockroach/` (identical SQL unless a CRDB-specific construct is documented).
184: 2. CI enforces parity (Section 8): same file lists, same statement counts.
185: 3. CRDB LATEST.sql is regenerated from postgres LATEST.sql by a documented script (`scripts/gen-crdb-latest.sh`) that applies ONLY the documented diffs in §2.2 — no manual divergence.
186: 4. All migration SQL must avoid CRDB-unsupported constructs: `CREATE EXTENSION`, `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, triggers, `ALTER COLUMN TYPE` (documented as restricted/limited on CRDB). CI greps for these (Section 8).
187: 
188: ### 2.2 LATEST.sql adaptations (postgres → cockroach)
189: 
190: **PK strategy — sequences, not `unique_rowid()` (C-new-1).**
191: 
192: - CRDB default `SERIAL` mode (`rowid`) produces 64-bit `unique_rowid()` values that overflow the codebase's `int32` ID structs. Therefore the cockroach LATEST.sql must force sequence-backed generation:
193:   - Add at the top of `LATEST.sql`:
194:     ```sql
195:     SET serial_normalization = sql_sequence;
196:     ```
197:     (per official SERIAL docs: `sql_sequence` mode creates a regular SQL sequence and `SERIAL` → `INT DEFAULT nextval(<seq>)`; values start small and remain int32-compatible.)
198:   - Or, if session-variable reliance is undesirable, spell it out per table:
199:     ```sql
200:     CREATE SEQUENCE "user_id_seq";
201:     CREATE TABLE "user" (
202:       id INT DEFAULT nextval('"user_id_seq"') PRIMARY KEY,
203:       ...
204:     );
205:     ```
206:   - **Decision:** prefer the `SET serial_normalization = sql_sequence` header (single statement, all ~50 SERIAL columns inherit it). Verify with `SHOW CREATE TABLE "user"` in `crdb:verify` that the default became `nextval(...)`, not `unique_rowid()`.
207: - **Documented trade-off (M-6, superseded by C-new-1):** sequence-backed IDs serialize nextval calls cluster-wide — a write bottleneck at very high throughput, and the opposite of CRDB's documented preference (`unique_rowid`/UUID scatter writes). Acceptable here because (a) int32 API/struct compatibility is mandatory, (b) this application's write volume is low. Follow-up item: widen ID columns to `INT8` + `unique_rowid()` when store structs move to `int64`.
208: 
209: Other adaptations:
210: 
211: | Postgres | Cockroach | Reason |
212: |----------|-----------|--------|
213: | `SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` | unchanged, with `SET serial_normalization = sql_sequence` header | int32-safe values (C-new-1) |
214: | `BIGINT` columns/defaults | unchanged (`INT`/`INT8` are the same type on CRDB) | alias identity |
215: | `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` defaults | unchanged; verify DECIMAL→INT assignment coercion in `crdb:verify`; cast `::BIGINT` only if coercion fails (M-1) | CRDB returns DECIMAL |
216: | `TEXT` columns | unchanged | `TEXT` is an alias of `STRING` |
217: | `JSONB DEFAULT '{}'` | unchanged | supported |
218: | `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` seed | unchanged | supported |
219: | `CREATE TABLE "user"` | unchanged | quoted identifier supported |
220: 
221: **Do NOT put `agent_vectors` into LATEST.sql** (H-3/ChatGPT): the table and its `VECTOR(1536)` index are CockroachDB-specific and build-tag-gated; migrations are shared with other drivers. Keep runtime creation in `CockroachVectorDB.Validate()` and document it as intentional.
222: 
223: ### 2.3 Migration execution mode (C-new-3, C-new-5, H-5)
224: 
225: The shared migrator (`store/migrator.go`) executes each migration file as **one multi-statement Exec inside one explicit transaction** (`tx.Begin()` → `execute()` → `tx.Commit()`). On CRDB this is the documented anti-pattern. Adaptation, confined to `s.profile.Driver == "cockroach"`:
226: 
227: 1. **Split migration files into individual statements** (respecting string literals/comments; add a small splitter in `store/migrator.go` or `store/migration_helper.go`).
228: 2. **Execute each statement as its own implicit transaction** (no wrapping `sql.Tx` for the cockroach driver). This:
229:    - avoids "DDL inside multi-statement transaction can fail while other statements succeed" (v25.x Known Limitations),
230:    - avoids the extended-protocol multi-statement limitation (each statement is small enough for any protocol),
231:    - keeps the existing `execute()` tolerance for "duplicate column/already exists" per statement.
232: 3. **Never wrap migration execution in `crdb.ExecuteTx`** (C-new-5) — schema-change transactions cannot be retried; fail cleanly with the original error and let the operator fix and restart.
233: 4. Keep the existing single-transaction behavior for `sqlite`/`postgres`/`mysql` unchanged.
234:

304: ## 4. Transaction Retry Strategy (H-4, C-new-5, isolation)
305: 
306: CRDB default isolation is SERIALIZABLE and signals retry with SQLSTATE **40001** + message starting "restart transaction" (`prod_checklist.md:649`; official transaction-retry docs). Client-side retry is mandatory.
307: 
308: ### 4.1 Inventory (verified)
309: 
310: | Site | File:line | Pattern | CRDB action |
311: |------|-----------|---------|-------------|
312: | CreateAgentMessages | `agent.go:772` | `BeginTx` + insert loop + Commit | wrap in `withTx` |
313: | CreateBridgeHandoffReplyIfActive | `bridge.go:356` | `conn.BeginTx` + `SELECT…FOR UPDATE` + INSERT + Commit | wrap in `withTx` |
314: | CreateBridgeHandoffReplyAndOutboxIfActive | `bridge.go:500` | same pattern | wrap in `withTx` |
315: | EnsureBridgeExternalSession | `bridge.go:112` | `BeginTx` upsert | wrap in `withTx` |
316: | (remaining bridge sites) | `bridge.go:726,818,912,1003` | `BeginTx` + Commit | wrap in `withTx` |
317: | ClaimPendingEvents | `agent.go:2781` (no tx wrapper; single `UPDATE…FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED…RETURNING`) | single statement | retryable via `RunResiliently`-style 40001 handling or `withTx`; SKIP LOCKED supported on v25.x |
318: 
319: ### 4.2 `withTx` helper (cockroach variant only)
320: 
321: Refactor the 8 `BeginTx` sites to closure form through a helper that, in cockroach mode, uses `crdb.ExecuteTx` (from `github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach-go/v2/crdb`, already in go.mod v2.4.3 — the same library the pgx tutorial uses via `crdbpgxv5`; `pgx.md:315-365`):
322: 
323: ```go
324: // postgres/resilience.go
325: func (d *DB) withTx(ctx context.Context, fn func(tx *sql.Tx) error) error {
326:     if !d.isCockroach {
327:         tx, err := d.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
328:         if err != nil { return err }
329:         defer tx.Rollback()
330:         if err := fn(tx); err != nil { return err }
331:         return tx.Commit()
332:     }
333:     return crdb.ExecuteTx(ctx, d.db, nil, fn) // retries SQLSTATE 40001
334: }
335: ```
336: 
337: - `crdb.ExecuteTx` works with both `*sql.DB` and `*sql.Conn` (both satisfy its executor interface); keep `conn.BeginTx` sites working via the same helper.
338: - **Constraint:** `fn` must be re-runnable — no side effects outside the transaction (verified: all 8 sites are pure read-modify-write within the tx).
339: - **Explicitly excluded:** `store/migrator.go` (C-new-5).
340:

414: ## 7. Risks & Mitigations (revised)
415: 
416: | Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
417: |------|----------|------------|
418: | 64-bit CRDB row IDs overflow `int32` structs (C-new-1) | Critical | `SET serial_normalization = sql_sequence` in CRDB LATEST.sql; verify via `SHOW CREATE`; add scan regression test |
419: | Migrator fails to boot without versioned dirs (C-new-2) | Critical | `migration/cockroach/0.35/1__init.sql` marker + parity CI |
420: | Migration multi-statement Exec breaks without simple protocol (C-new-3) | High | Keep `default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol`; statement-level execution for CRDB |
421: | DDL inside single explicit tx can partially fail at COMMIT (H-5) | High | Statement-per-implicit-transaction execution for cockroach driver |
422: | 40001 serialization errors on hot paths | High | `withTx` → `crdb.ExecuteTx` for the 8 inventory sites; never for migrations |
423: | `DATABASE_URL` fallback misconfigures cockroach driver (C-4) | High | `COCKROACH_DSN` required, no fallback, loud startup error |
424: | Local compose lacks DB/user bootstrap (C-new-4) | High | `COCKROACH_DATABASE/USER/PASSWORD` envs in compose |
425: | Connection pool exceeds 4× cluster vCPUs (H-1) | Medium | `COCKROACH_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` default 8 for 2-vCPU CRDB Cloud |
426: | `unique_rowid()` hotspots (M-6) | Low (accepted) | Sequences chosen for int32 compatibility; documented; int64 follow-up |
427: | `EXTRACT(EPOCH)` DECIMAL→INT coercion (M-1) | Low | verify-first; cast in LATEST.sql only if needed |
428: | `::BIGINT`/JSONB/ILIKE edge differences | Low | `crdb:verify` battery covers each construct (0.3) |
429: | First-deploy empty RAG index (M-3) | Medium | `FORCE_REINDEX_ON_STARTUP=true` on deploy #1 |
430: | Placeholder secrets (M-4) | Medium | parameterized script, `set -euo pipefail`, no defaults for DSN/key |

25: ## 1. Critical Findings (Block Implementation)
26: 
27: ### C-1: Code Duplication Without Abstraction
28: 
29: **Severity:** CRITICAL
30: **Location:** Plan Section 1.4
31: 
32: The plan copies ~22 files from `store/db/postgres/` to `store/db/cockroach/` with only "package name change" and minor edits. This creates a **maintenance fork**:
33: 
34: - Every bug fix in `postgres/` must be manually duplicated in `cockroach/`
35: - Every new feature must be implemented twice
36: - Schema changes in `LATEST.sql` require updates in two places
37: - Risk of drift between postgres and cockroach implementations grows over time
38: 
39: The ChatGPT review called this "the biggest issue in the whole review" and "a long-term maintenance nightmare." I agree.
40: 
41: **Recommended Fix:**
42: - **Option A (Preferred):** Create a shared `store/db/common/` package with all SQL-agnostic logic. Both `postgres` and `cockroach` packages import and wrap it, providing only driver-specific connection setup and resilience.
43: - **Option B:** Use Go build tags within a single `store/db/postgres/` package, similar to the `vectordb_cockroach.go` / `vectordb_nocockroach.go` pattern.
44: - **Option C (Minimum):** Add a CI check that diffs the two packages and fails if they diverge by more than the expected resilience differences.

50: **Severity:** CRITICAL

54: 
55: | Missing File | Purpose |
56: |--------------|---------|
57: | `bridge_auth.go` | Bridge authentication store methods |
58: | `memo_relation.go` | Memo relationship store methods |

60: **Impact:** Compile errors when building the cockroach driver.

73: The plan focuses almost entirely on `LATEST.sql` and does not address:
74: - How incremental migrations will be maintained for CRDB
75: - Whether existing Postgres incremental migrations are compatible with CockroachDB
76: - What happens if a future migration uses Postgres-specific syntax

78: Without a documented process, Cockroach support will slowly rot after initial implementation.

92: The plan proposes:

96:     p.DSN = os.Getenv("COCKROACH_DSN")
97:     if p.DSN == "" {

117: The plan states store methods are "SQL-agnostic" and can be copied verbatim. CockroachDB officially states:
118: 
119: > PostgreSQL compatibility is high, but not complete. Applications should expect to rewrite unsupported SQL constructs.
120: 
121: The plan does not verify this claim with an actual audit of the store files.
122: 
123: **Required Audit:**
124: ```bash
125: grep -rn '::BIGINT\|::INT\|::TEXT\|::UUID\|::JSONB\|::BYTEA\|::TIMESTAMPTZ' store/db/postgres/
126: ```
127: 
128: **Note on `::BIGINT`:** CockroachDB officially supports `BIGINT` as an alias for `INT8`. The specific cast syntax `::BIGINT` is used in `store/db/postgres/agent.go`. This must be **verified against a running CRDB instance**, not assumed to work or fail. The original review claimed `::BIGINT` is unsupported; this is **not established** by available documentation. Downgrade to MEDIUM pending verification.

132: ## 2. High Findings (Must Fix Before Production)
133: 
134: ### H-1: Connection Pool Settings Exceed CRDB Recommendations
135: 
136: **Severity:** HIGH
137: **Location:** Plan Section 1.1 (`cockroach.go`)
138: 
139: The plan copies `SetMaxOpenConns(10)` from the Postgres driver. Official CockroachDB documentation states:
140: 
141: > The number of active connections across all connection pools should not exceed 4 times the number of vCPUs in the cluster by a large amount.
142: 
143: For a Fly.io shared-cpu-1x instance (1 vCPU), the maximum recommended connections is **4**. Setting `MaxOpenConns=10` will cause connection exhaustion, queueing, and degraded performance.
144: 
145: **Official Reference:** `bugs/057/prod_checklist.md` — Connection pooling section
146: 
147: **Recommended Fix:**
148: ```go
149: // Make pool settings configurable
150: maxOpenConns := 4 // Default for 1 vCPU; scale with CRDB node size
151: if cpuCount := runtime.NumCPU(); cpuCount > 1 {
152:     maxOpenConns = cpuCount * 4
153: }
154: db.SetMaxOpenConns(maxOpenConns)
155: ```
156: 
157: Or read from env var `COCKROACH_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` with sensible default.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### H-2: `sslmode=require` Is Insufficient for Production
162: 
163: **Severity:** HIGH
164: **Location:** Plan Section 4.4 (`scripts/fly-crdb-secrets.sh`)
165: 
166: The plan uses `sslmode=require`, which encrypts traffic but does **not** verify the server's certificate. Official CockroachDB documentation states:
167: 
168: > To deploy CockroachDB in production, it is strongly recommended to use TLS certificates to authenticate the identity of nodes and clients and to encrypt data in transit.
169: 
170: The Docker single-node example in `bugs/057/docker.md` uses `sslmode=verify-full` with certificate paths. The CockroachDB Cloud connection string example in `bugs/057/pgx.md` uses `sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=...`.
171: 
172: **Official References:**
173: - `bugs/057/prod_checklist.md` — Security section
174: - `bugs/057/docker.md` — secure mode examples
175: - `bugs/057/pgx.md` — Cloud connection string example
176: 
177: **Recommended Fix:**
178: ```bash
179: # For CRDB Cloud, use verify-full with CA cert
180: COCKROACH_DSN="postgresql://user:password@host:26257/db?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/path/to/ca.crt"
181: ```
182: 
183: For Fly.io deployment, store the CA cert as a secret or volume mount.
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ### H-3: Race Condition in `agent_vectors` Table Creation
188: 
189: **Severity:** HIGH
190: **Location:** Plan Section 1.1 (`vectordb_cockroach.go` referenced)
191: 
192: The plan states `agent_vectors` is created at runtime by `CockroachVectorDB.Validate()`. If multiple app instances start simultaneously (e.g., during Fly.io rollout), they will all attempt `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_vectors`. While `IF NOT EXISTS` prevents errors, concurrent `CREATE INDEX` statements could cause lock contention or schema validation failures.
193: 
194: Schema changes in CockroachDB can be asynchronous and involve job scheduling. Spreading schema creation across runtime paths is fragile.
195: 
196: **Recommended Fix:**
197: - Create `agent_vectors` in `LATEST.sql` instead of at runtime
198: - Or wrap runtime creation in `crdb.ExecuteTx` with retry logic
199: - Or add a distributed lock using CRDB's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ### H-4: Transaction Retry Semantics Not Fully Examined
204: 
205: **Severity:** HIGH
206: **Location:** Plan Section 1.1 (`resilience.go`)
207: 
208: The plan wraps transactions with `crdb.ExecuteTx` but does not examine whether existing transaction patterns in the codebase are compatible with CockroachDB's retry model. CockroachDB retries require careful handling of:
209: 
210: - Read-write conflicts
211: - SAVEPOINT semantics
212: - Transaction IDs and restarts
213: 
214: The official pgx tutorial (`bugs/057/pgx.md`) shows `crdbpgx.ExecuteTx` used for **every** transaction, including simple inserts. The plan must ensure all write transactions in the cockroach driver use the retry wrapper.
215: 
216: **Official Reference:** `bugs/057/pgx.md` — shows `crdbpgx.ExecuteTx` for all transactions
217: 
218: ---
219: 
220: ### H-5: Schema Change Behavior Not Addressed
221: 
222: **Severity:** HIGH
223: **Location:** Plan Section 2
224: 
225: CockroachDB schema changes are **asynchronous** in many cases. The plan assumes synchronous DDL like PostgreSQL. This could cause:
226: 
227: - Migrations appearing to complete before schema is fully applied
228: - Subsequent queries failing during schema change propagation
229: - Test flakiness if tests run immediately after migration
230: 
231: **Recommended Fix:**
232: - Add `SET CLUSTER SETTING jobs.registry.interval.gc = '30s'` during testing
233: - Add a post-migration verification step or wait mechanism
234: - Document that CRDB schema changes are asynchronous
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ### H-6: No Rollback Plan
239: 
240: **Severity:** HIGH
241: **Location:** Plan Section 4 (entire)
242: 
243: The plan has no rollback strategy if CockroachDB deployment fails after the Postgres deployment is working.
244: 
245: **Recommended Fix:**
246: - Add a rollback section:
247:   - How to revert to Postgres if CRDB Cloud is unreachable
248:   - Fly.io `fly deploy -c fly_pg.toml` as rollback command
249:   - Data migration strategy if data exists in CRDB
250: - Add a canary deployment strategy: deploy to staging first, validate, then promote to production
251:

256: ### M-1: `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` Type Mismatch in LATEST.sql
257: 
258: **Severity:** MEDIUM
259: **Location:** Plan Section 2.2
260: 
261: The plan uses `extract(epoch from now())` for `INT` columns. In CockroachDB, `extract(epoch from now())` returns `double precision`. Inserting a `double precision` into an `INT` column may fail or cause implicit truncation.

263: **Recommended Fix:**
264: ```sql

287: **Severity:** MEDIUM
288: **Location:** Plan Section 4.2

51: 
52: #### DSN Flow
53: 
54: ```
55: fly secrets set DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
56:     │
57:     ▼
58: Docker container starts, entrypoint.sh runs
59:     │  (file_env expands MEMOS_DSN_FILE if present)
60:     ▼
61: bin/memos/main.go → viper reads MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres from [env]
62:     │

65:     │
66:     ▼

68:     │
69:     ▼
70: store/db/postgres/postgres.go: sql.Open("pgx", profile.DSN + "?default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol")
71:     │
72:     ▼
73: pgx/v5 handles sslmode=require natively for Neon
74: ```

76: #### Driver: pgx/v5 via database/sql stdlib adapter
77: 
78: ```go
79: // store/db/postgres/postgres.go
80: import _ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"
81: 
82: func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
83:     dsn := profile.DSN
84:     // Auto-append simple_protocol for Neon PgBouncer compatibility
85:     if !strings.Contains(dsn, "default_query_exec_mode") {
86:         sep := "?"
87:         if strings.Contains(dsn, "?") { sep = "&" }
88:         dsn += sep + "default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol"
89:     }
90:     db, err := sql.Open("pgx", dsn)
91:     db.SetMaxOpenConns(10)
92:     db.SetMaxIdleConns(5)
93:     db.SetConnMaxLifetime(5 * time.Minute)
94:     db.SetConnMaxIdleTime(1 * time.Minute)
95:     return &DB{db: db, profile: profile}, nil
96: }
97: ```

128: ### 2.3 CockroachDB Best Practices
129: 
130: From `/home/chaschel/Desktop/cockroach/best-practices/`:
131: 
132: **prod_checklist.md:**
133: - Transaction retry handling is MANDATORY (client-side, SQLSTATE 40001)
134: - Connection pooling: active connections ≤ 4x vCPU count
135: - TLS certificates required for all production connections
136: - `--cache=.25 --max-sql-memory=.25` (defaults are too low)
137: - Use `--locality` flag on all nodes
138: 
139: **test_locally.md:**
140: ```bash
141: cockroach start-single-node --insecure --store=type=mem,size=0.25 --advertise-addr=localhost
142: # Recommended cluster settings for faster testing:
143: SET CLUSTER SETTING kv.range_merge.queue_interval = '50ms';
144: SET CLUSTER SETTING jobs.registry.interval.gc = '30s';
145: SET CLUSTER SETTING jobs.retention_time = '15s';
146: SET CLUSTER SETTING sql.stats.automatic_collection.enabled = false;
147: ALTER RANGE default CONFIGURE ZONE USING "gc.ttlseconds" = 600;
148: ```
149: 
150: **docker.md:**
151: - Uses Docker bridge network and volumes for data persistence
152: - Insecure mode is for non-production testing only
153: - Single-node supports auto-creating database/user/password via environment variables
154: - Graceful shutdown recommended with 5-minute timeout
155: 
156: ### 2.4 CockroachDB Postgres Compatibility
157: 
158: CockroachDB is wire-compatible with PostgreSQL. Key compatibility notes:
159: 
160: | Feature | CockroachDB | Notes |
161: |---------|-------------|-------|
162: | `SERIAL` | Supported | But `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid()` preferred for performance |
163: | `INT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` | Supported | Preferred over SERIAL |
164: | `JSONB` | Supported | Works as-is |
165: | `BYTEA` | Supported | Works as-is |
166: | `BOOLEAN` | Supported | Works as-is |
167: | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Supported | Works as-is |
168: | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | Supported | Works as-is |
169: | `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` | Supported | Works as-is |
170: | `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` | Supported | Works as-is |
171: | `ON CONFLICT (col) DO UPDATE SET` | Supported | Works as-is |
172: | `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` | Supported | Works as-is |
173: | Foreign keys | Supported | Works as-is |
174: | CHECK constraints | Supported | Works as-is |
175: | `pgx/v5` driver | Supported | Wire-compatible |
176: | SQLSTATE 40001 | Serialization error | Must handle with client-side retry |
177: | `CREATE EXTENSION` | NOT supported | No extension system |
178: | `pgvector` | NOT supported | Use native `VECTOR` type instead |

216: | `store/db/cockroach/cockroach.go` | Driver init: `sql.Open("pgx", dsn)` — no `default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol` (not needed for CRDB) |
217: | `store/db/cockroach/migration_history.go` | Migration history CRUD (adapted from postgres) |
218: | `store/db/cockroach/common.go` | Placeholder helpers (`$1`, `$2`, ...) |
219: | `store/db/cockroach/resilience.go` | Transient error detection + `crdb.ExecuteTx` wrapper for SQLSTATE 40001 |
220: | `store/db/cockroach/activity.go` | Activity store methods |
221: | `store/db/cockroach/agent.go` | Agent store methods |
222: | `store/db/cockroach/bridge.go` | Bridge store methods |
223: | `store/db/cockroach/memo.go` | Memo store methods |
224: | `store/db/cockroach/ticket.go` | Ticket store methods |
225: | `store/db/cockroach/user.go` | User store methods |
226: | `store/db/cockroach/resource.go` | Resource store methods |
227: | `store/db/cockroach/inbox.go` | Inbox store methods |
228: | `store/db/cockroach/webhook.go` | Webhook store methods |
229: | `store/db/cockroach/reaction.go` | Reaction store methods |
230: | `store/db/cockroach/rbac.go` | RBAC store methods |
231: | `store/db/cockroach/notification.go` | Notification store methods |
232: | `store/db/cockroach/workspace_setting.go` | Workspace settings |
233: | `store/db/cockroach/user_setting.go` | User settings |
234: | `store/db/cockroach/idp.go` | Identity provider |
235: | `store/db/cockroach/memo_filter.go` | Memo filtering |
236: | `store/db/cockroach/agent_observations.go` | Agent observations |
237: | `store/db/cockroach/agent_workflow.go` | Agent workflows |
238: 
239: #### 1.2 Key Differences from Postgres Driver
240: 
241: **`cockroach.go` (driver init):**
242: ```go
243: func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
244:     dsn := profile.DSN
245:     // NO default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol — not needed for CockroachDB
246:     db, err := sql.Open("pgx", dsn)
247:     db.SetMaxOpenConns(10)
248:     db.SetMaxIdleConns(5)
249:     db.SetConnMaxLifetime(5 * time.Minute)
250:     db.SetConnMaxIdleTime(1 * time.Minute)
251:     return &DB{db: db, profile: profile}, nil
252: }
253: ```
254: 
255: **`resilience.go` (transaction retry):**
256: ```go
257: import "github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach-go/v2/crdb"
258: 
259: // ExecuteTx wraps crdb.ExecuteTx for automatic retry on SQLSTATE 40001
260: func ExecuteTx(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, fn func(tx *sql.Tx) error) error {
261:     return crdb.ExecuteTx(ctx, db, nil, fn)
262: }
263: ```
264: 
265: #### 1.3 Modify Existing Files
266: 
267: | File | Change |
268: |------|--------|
269: | `store/db/db.go` | Add `case "cockroach":` to switch, import cockroach package |
270: | `internal/profile/profile.go` | Add cockroach driver case: read DSN from `COCKROACH_DSN` env var with `DATABASE_URL` fallback |
271: 
272: **`profile.go` addition:**
273: ```go
274: if p.Driver == "cockroach" && p.DSN == "" {
275:     p.DSN = os.Getenv("COCKROACH_DSN")
276:     if p.DSN == "" {
277:         p.DSN = os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")  // fallback for consistency
278:     }
279:     if p.DSN == "" {
280:         return errors.New("cockroach driver requires COCKROACH_DSN or DATABASE_URL environment variable")
281:     }
282: }
283: ```
284: 
285: **`db.go` addition:**
286: ```go
287: import "github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/cockroach"
288: 
289: case "cockroach":
290:     driver, err = cockroach.NewDB(profile)
291: ```
292: 
293: #### 1.4 Method Migration Strategy
294: 
295: The postgres store methods are SQL-agnostic (they use `$1`, `$2` placeholders which work in both Postgres and CockroachDB). The migration approach:
296: 
297: 1. Copy all `.go` files from `store/db/postgres/` to `store/db/cockroach/`
298: 2. Change package name from `postgres` to `cockroach`
299: 3. Replace `isTransientError` with CockroachDB-aware version (add SQLSTATE 40001)
300: 4. Replace direct `tx.ExecContext` calls in transaction-heavy methods with `crdb.ExecuteTx` wrapper
301: 5. Remove `default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol` from connection setup
302: 
303: **Estimated effort:** ~22 files to copy and adapt. Most are direct copies with package name change.
304:

306: 
307: ### Phase 2: Migration Schema (`store/migration/cockroach/`)
308: 
309: **Goal:** Create a CockroachDB-specific LATEST.sql that optimizes for CRDB performance characteristics.
310: 
311: #### 2.1 New File
312: 
313: | File | Purpose |
314: |------|---------|
315: | `store/migration/cockroach/LATEST.sql` | Full schema adapted for CockroachDB |
316: 
317: #### 2.2 Key Adaptations from Postgres LATEST.sql
318: 
319: ```sql
320: -- =====================================================
321: -- COCKROACHDB SCHEMA (adapted from Postgres LATEST.sql)
322: -- =====================================================
323: 
324: -- migration_history
325: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration_history (
326:   version TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
327:   created_ts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now())
328: );
329: 
330: -- user
331: -- SERIAL → INT DEFAULT unique_rowid() for better CRDB performance
332: CREATE TABLE "user" (
333:   id INT DEFAULT unique_rowid() PRIMARY KEY,
334:   created_ts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now()),
335:   updated_ts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now()),
336:   row_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (row_status IN ('NORMAL', 'ARCHIVED')) DEFAULT 'NORMAL',
337:   username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
338:   role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('HOST', 'ADMIN', 'USER')) DEFAULT 'USER',
339:   email TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
340:   nickname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
341:   password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
342:   avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
343:   description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
344:   allowed_tenant_ids TEXT DEFAULT NULL
345: );
346: 
347: -- memo
348: CREATE TABLE memo (
349:   id INT DEFAULT unique_rowid() PRIMARY KEY,
350:   uid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
351:   creator_id INT NOT NULL,
352:   created_ts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now()),
353:   updated_ts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now()),
354:   row_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (row_status IN ('NORMAL', 'ARCHIVED')) DEFAULT 'NORMAL',
355:   content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
356:   visibility TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (visibility IN ('PUBLIC', 'PROTECTED', 'PRIVATE')) DEFAULT 'PRIVATE',
357:   pinned BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
358:   payload JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
359:   tenant_id INT DEFAULT NULL
360: );
361: 
362: -- ... (all other tables follow same pattern)
363: -- SERIAL → INT DEFAULT unique_rowid()
364: -- INTEGER → INT
365: -- BIGINT → INT (CRDB handles large ints natively)
366: -- Everything else stays the same
367: ```
368: 
369: #### 2.3 DDL Differences Summary
370: 
371: | Postgres | CockroachDB | Reason |
372: |----------|-------------|--------|
373: | `SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` | `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid() PRIMARY KEY` | Better performance, avoids sequence contention |
374: | `INTEGER` | `INT` | Idiomatic CRDB (both work) |
375: | `BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` | `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT extract(epoch from now())` | CRDB INT handles 64-bit |
376: | `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT` | `extract(epoch from now())` | No cast needed |
377: | Everything else | Same | CRDB is wire-compatible |
378: 
379: #### 2.4 Seed Data
380: 
381: The `tenant_role_templates` INSERT in LATEST.sql uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — this works in CockroachDB as-is.

614: 
615: ## 4. Risks & Mitigations
616: 
617: | Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
618: |------|----------|------------|
619: | `SERIAL` sequence contention on CRDB | Medium | Use `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid()` in LATEST.sql |
620: | SQLSTATE 40001 serialization errors | High | Wrap all write transactions with `crdb.ExecuteTx` |
621: | `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT` cast | Low | Test in local — CRDB supports this syntax |
622: | `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` | Low | Verified — works in CRDB |
623: | Connection pooling limits | Medium | CRDB recommends max 4x vCPU connections; pgx pool settings |
624: | CGO for LanceDB in Dockerfile | Low | Keep CGO_ENABLED=1; CRDB vector is pure Go via cockroach-go |
625: | `agent_vectors` table creation timing | Medium | Validate() creates it — ensure it runs before first vector operation |
626: | `migration_helper.go` SQLite-only functions | Low | Already gated on `s.profile.Driver == "sqlite"` — no change needed |

10: ## 1. Critical Findings (Must Fix Before Implementation)

12: ### C-1: Postgres-Specific Cast Syntax in Go Store Code
13: 
14: **Severity:** CRITICAL
15: **Location:** `store/db/postgres/agent.go` lines 2605, 2693, 2718, 2776, 2780
16: 
17: The plan states that store methods are "SQL-agnostic" and can be copied verbatim. This is **false**. The `agent.go` file hardcodes Postgres-specific cast syntax:
18: 
19: ```go
20: // line 2605
21: VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT)
22: 
23: // line 2776
24: SET status = 'processing', claimed_at = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT, attempts = attempts + 1
25: ```
26: 
27: **Problem:** CockroachDB does not support `::BIGINT` cast syntax. It uses `::INT` or `CAST(... AS INT)`. Additionally, `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` returns `double precision` in CRDB, not `bigint`.
28: 
29: **Impact:** Runtime SQL errors on every insert/update in `agent.go` and any other file using this pattern.
30: 
31: **Recommended Fix:**
32: - Search all postgres store files for `::BIGINT`, `::INT`, `::TEXT`, `::BOOLEAN` casts
33: - Replace with CRDB-compatible syntax or remove unnecessary casts
34: - For `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` results, use `CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW()) AS INT)` or rely on implicit cast if column type is INT
35: - Add a grep-based audit step: `grep -rn '::[A-Z]' store/db/postgres/`

82: ### H-1: Connection Pool Settings Exceed CRDB Cloud Recommendations
83: 
84: **Severity:** HIGH
85: **Location:** Plan Section 1.1 (`cockroach.go`)
86: 
87: The plan copies `SetMaxOpenConns(10)` from the Postgres driver. CRDB best practices state:
88: 
89: > active connections ≤ 4x vCPU count
90: 
91: For a Fly.io shared-cpu-1x instance (1 vCPU), the maximum recommended connections is **4**. Setting `MaxOpenConns=10` will cause connection exhaustion, queueing, and degraded performance.
92: 
93: **Recommended Fix:**
94: ```go

96: maxOpenConns := 4 // Default for 1 vCPU; scale with CRDB node size
97: if cpuCount := runtime.NumCPU(); cpuCount > 1 {
98:     maxOpenConns = cpuCount * 4
99: }
100: db.SetMaxOpenConns(maxOpenConns)
101: ```
102: 
103: Or read from env var `CRDB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` with sensible default.

107: ### H-2: `COCKROACH_DSN` / `DATABASE_URL` Fallback Is Dangerous
108: 
109: **Severity:** HIGH
110: **Location:** Plan Section 1.3 (`internal/profile/profile.go`)
111: 
112: ```go

114:     p.DSN = os.Getenv("COCKROACH_DSN")
115:     if p.DSN == "" {
116:         p.DSN = os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")  // fallback for consistency
117:     }

119: ```
120: 
121: If an operator has `DATABASE_URL` set for Postgres (e.g., from a previous deployment) and accidentally sets `MEMOS_DRIVER=cockroach`, the app will connect to the Postgres database using the cockroach driver. This could cause silent data corruption or schema conflicts.
122: 
123: **Recommended Fix:**
124: - Remove the `DATABASE_URL` fallback for the `cockroach` driver
125: - Require explicit `COCKROACH_DSN` to prevent accidental misconfiguration

131: 
132: **Severity:** HIGH
133: **Location:** Plan Section 4.4 (`scripts/fly-crdb-secrets.sh`)
134: 
135: The plan uses `sslmode=require`, which encrypts traffic but does **not** verify the server's certificate. This is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.
136: 
137: CRDB best practices state:
138: > TLS certificates required for all production connections
139: 
140: **Recommended Fix:**
141: ```bash
142: # For CRDB Cloud, download the CA certificate
143: cockroach cert create-ca --certs-dir=/certs --ca-key=ca.key
144: 
145: # Or use sslmode=verify-full with sslrootcert
146: COCKROACH_DSN="postgresql://user:password@host:26257/db?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/path/to/ca.crt"
147: ```
148: 
149: For Fly.io deployment, store the CA cert as a secret or volume mount.

154: 
155: **Severity:** HIGH
156: **Location:** Plan Section 1.1 (`vectordb_cockroach.go` referenced)
157: 
158: The plan states `agent_vectors` is created at runtime by `CockroachVectorDB.Validate()`. If multiple app instances start simultaneously (e.g., during Fly.io rollout), they will all attempt `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_vectors`. While `IF NOT EXISTS` prevents errors, concurrent `CREATE INDEX` statements could cause lock contention or schema validation failures.
159: 
160: **Recommended Fix:**

162: - Or add a distributed lock using CRDB's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`
163: - Or create `agent_vectors` in `LATEST.sql` instead of at runtime

184: ### M-2: `unique_rowid()` Write Hotspots Not Addressed
185: 
186: **Severity:** MEDIUM
187: **Location:** Plan Section 2.2
188: 
189: The plan replaces `SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` with `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid() PRIMARY KEY`. While `unique_rowid()` avoids sequence contention, it generates timestamp-based IDs that cause write hotspots on the same range for high-throughput tables.
190: 
191: **Impact:** Tables with high insert rates (e.g., `agent_messages`, `agent_events`) may experience write contention.
192: 
193: **Recommended Fix:**
194: - Use `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid()` for most tables
195: - For very high-throughput tables, consider `UUID` primary keys (supported by CRDB)
196: - Document the trade-off in the plan
197: - Consider `ALTER TABLE ... CONFIGURE ZONE` with specific replica placement for hotspot tables

35: This tutorial shows you how build a simple CRUD Go application with CockroachDB and the [Go pgx driver](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx).
36: 
37: ## Step 1. Start CockroachDB
38: 
39: <Tabs>
40:   <Tab title="Use CockroachDB Cloud">
41:     ### Choose your installation method
42:

54:         2. [Log in](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/) to your CockroachDB Cloud account.
55:         3. On the **Clusters** page, click **Create cluster**.
56:         4. On the **Select a plan** page, select **Basic**.
57:         5. On the **Cloud & Regions** page, select a cloud provider (GCP or AWS) in the **Cloud provider** section.
58:         6. In the **Regions** section, select a region for the cluster. Refer to <InternalLink version="cockroachcloud" path="regions">CockroachDB Cloud Regions</InternalLink> for the regions where CockroachDB Basic clusters can be deployed. To create a multi-region cluster, click **Add region** and select additional regions.
59:         7. Click **Next: Capacity**.

63:            Your cluster will be created in a few seconds and the **Create SQL user** dialog will display.

If you forget your password, you can reset it by going to the **SQL Users** page for the cluster, found at `https://cockroachlabs.cloud/cluster/<CLUSTER ID>/users`.

194: ## Step 2. Get the code
195: 
196: Clone the code's GitHub repo:
197:

209: The `main.go` file contains the code for `CREATE TABLE`, `INSERT`, `SELECT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` SQL operations. The file also executes the `main` method of the program.
210: 
211: ```go theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-mocha","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
212: package main

223: func initTable(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx) error {
224: 	// Dropping existing table if it exists
225: 	log.Println("Drop existing accounts table if necessary.")
226: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS accounts"); err != nil {
227: 		return err
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	// Create the accounts table
231: 	log.Println("Creating accounts table.")
232: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
233: 		"CREATE TABLE accounts (id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), balance INT8)"); err != nil {
234: 		return err
235: 	}
236: 	return nil
237: }
238: 
239: func insertRows(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, accts [4]uuid.UUID) error {
240: 	// Insert four rows into the "accounts" table.
241: 	log.Println("Creating new rows...")
242: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
243: 		"INSERT INTO accounts (id, balance) VALUES ($1, $2), ($3, $4), ($5, $6), ($7, $8)", accts[0], 250, accts[1], 100, accts[2], 500, accts[3], 300); err != nil {
244: 		return err
245: 	}
246: 	return nil
247: }
248: 
249: func printBalances(conn *pgx.Conn) error {
250: 	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(), "SELECT id, balance FROM accounts")
251: 	if err != nil {
252: 		log.Fatal(err)
253: 	}
254: 	defer rows.Close()
255: 	for rows.Next() {
256: 		var id uuid.UUID
257: 		var balance int
258: 		if err := rows.Scan(&id, &balance); err != nil {
259: 			log.Fatal(err)
260: 		}
261: 		log.Printf("%s: %d\n", id, balance)
262: 	}
263: 	return nil
264: }
265: 
266: func transferFunds(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, from uuid.UUID, to uuid.UUID, amount int) error {
267: 	// Read the balance.
268: 	var fromBalance int
269: 	if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx,
270: 		"SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = $1", from).Scan(&fromBalance); err != nil {
271: 		return err
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	if fromBalance < amount {
275: 		log.Println("insufficient funds")
276: 	}
277: 
278: 	// Perform the transfer.
279: 	log.Printf("Transferring funds from account with ID %s to account with ID %s...", from, to)
280: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
281: 		"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - $1 WHERE id = $2", amount, from); err != nil {
282: 		return err
283: 	}
284: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
285: 		"UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + $1 WHERE id = $2", amount, to); err != nil {
286: 		return err
287: 	}
288: 	return nil
289: }
290: 
291: func deleteRows(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, one uuid.UUID, two uuid.UUID) error {
292: 	// Delete two rows into the "accounts" table.
293: 	log.Printf("Deleting rows with IDs %s and %s...", one, two)
294: 	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
295: 		"DELETE FROM accounts WHERE id IN ($1, $2)", one, two); err != nil {
296: 		return err
297: 	}
298: 	return nil
299: }

301: func main() {

303: 	config, err := pgx.ParseConfig(os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
304: 	if err != nil {
305: 		log.Fatal(err)
306: 	}
307: 	config.RuntimeParams["application_name"] = "$ docs_simplecrud_gopgx"
308: 	conn, err := pgx.ConnectConfig(context.Background(), config)
309: 	if err != nil {
310: 		log.Fatal(err)
311: 	}
312: 	defer conn.Close(context.Background())
313: 
314: 	// Set up table
315: 	err = crdbpgx.ExecuteTx(context.Background(), conn, pgx.TxOptions{}, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
316: 		return initTable(context.Background(), tx)
317: 	})
318: 
319: 	// Insert initial rows
320: 	var accounts [4]uuid.UUID
321: 	for i := 0; i < len(accounts); i++ {
322: 		accounts[i] = uuid.New()
323: 	}
324: 
325: 	err = crdbpgx.ExecuteTx(context.Background(), conn, pgx.TxOptions{}, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
326: 		return insertRows(context.Background(), tx, accounts)
327: 	})
328: 	if err == nil {
329: 		log.Println("New rows created.")

332: 	}
333: 
334: 	// Print out the balances

337: 
338: 	// Run a transfer
339: 	err = crdbpgx.ExecuteTx(context.Background(), conn, pgx.TxOptions{}, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
340: 		return transferFunds(context.Background(), tx, accounts[2], accounts[1], 100)
341: 	})
342: 	if err == nil {
343: 		log.Println("Transfer successful.")
344: 	} else {
345: 		log.Fatal("error: ", err)
346: 	}
347: 
348: 	// Print out the balances
349: 	log.Println("Balances after transfer:")
350: 	printBalances(conn)
351: 
352: 	// Delete rows
353: 	err = crdbpgx.ExecuteTx(context.Background(), conn, pgx.TxOptions{}, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
354: 		return deleteRows(context.Background(), tx, accounts[0], accounts[1])
355: 	})
356: 	if err == nil {

358: 	} else {

360: 	}
361: 
362: 	// Print out the balances

209: func (s *Store) getMigrationBasePath() string {
210: 	return fmt.Sprintf("migration/%s/", s.profile.Driver)
211: }

213: func (s *Store) getSeedBasePath() string {

217: func (s *Store) seed(ctx context.Context) error {
218: 	// Only seed for SQLite.
219: 	if s.profile.Driver != "sqlite" {
220: 		slog.Warn("seed is only supported for SQLite")
221: 		return nil
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	filenames, err := fs.Glob(seedFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*.sql", s.getSeedBasePath()))
225: 	if err != nil {
226: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read seed files")
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	// Sort seed files by name. This is important to ensure that seed files are applied in order.
230: 	sort.Strings(filenames)
231: 	// Start a transaction to apply the seed files.
232: 	tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
233: 	if err != nil {
234: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
235: 	}
236: 	defer tx.Rollback()
237: 	// Loop over all seed files and execute them in order.
238: 	for _, filename := range filenames {
239: 		bytes, err := seedFS.ReadFile(filename)
240: 		if err != nil {
241: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read seed file, filename=%s", filename)
242: 		}
243: 		if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
244: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "seed error: %s", filename)
245: 		}
246: 	}
247: 	return tx.Commit()
248: }
249: 
250: // GetCurrentSchemaVersion scans ALL migration subdirectories in the embedded FS
251: // to find the highest version file. The filesystem is the single source of truth.
252: //
253: // NOTE: This function does NOT call itself recursively. The */*.sql glob does NOT
254: // match LATEST.sql (which sits at the base path, not inside a subdirectory).
255: // getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript() calls GetCurrentSchemaVersion() when it
256: // encounters LATEST.sql, but that path is never reached from this glob.
257: func (s *Store) GetCurrentSchemaVersion() (string, error) {
258: 	filePaths, err := fs.Glob(MigrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
259: 	if err != nil {
260: 		return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to glob migration files")
261: 	}
262: 	if len(filePaths) == 0 {
263: 		return "", errors.Errorf("no migration files found in %s", s.getMigrationBasePath())
264: 	}
265: 	sort.Strings(filePaths) // fs.Glob does not guarantee sorted order
266: 
267: 	var maxVersion string
268: 	for _, filePath := range filePaths {
269: 		fileVer, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
270: 		if err != nil {
271: 			continue // skip files that can't be parsed (e.g., LATEST.sql at base path)
272: 		}
273: 		if maxVersion == "" || version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileVer, maxVersion) {
274: 			maxVersion = fileVer
275: 		}
276: 	}
277: 	if maxVersion == "" {
278: 		return "", errors.Errorf("could not determine schema version from migration files")
279: 	}
280: 	return maxVersion, nil
281: }
282: 
283: func (s *Store) validateSchemaVersionConsistency() error {
284: 	fsVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
285: 	if err != nil {
286: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get FS schema version")
287: 	}
288: 	codeVersion := version.GetCurrentVersion(s.profile.Mode)
289: 	codeMinor := version.GetMinorVersion(codeVersion)
290: 	fsMinor := version.GetMinorVersion(fsVersion)
291: 
292: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fsMinor, codeMinor) {
293: 		slog.Warn("migration FS has directories newer than code version; bump Version/DevVersion",
294: 			"fs_minor", fsMinor, "code_minor", codeMinor,
295: 			"fs_version", fsVersion, "code_version", codeVersion)
296: 	}
297: 	return nil // warn-only at runtime; build-time gate catches this earlier
298: }
299: 
300: func (s *Store) getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath string) (string, error) {
301: 	// If the file is the latest schema file, return the current schema version.
302: 	if strings.HasSuffix(filePath, LatestSchemaFileName) {
303: 		return s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
304: 	}
305: 
306: 	normalizedPath := filepath.ToSlash(filePath)
307: 	elements := strings.Split(normalizedPath, "/")
308: 	if len(elements) < 2 {
309: 		return "", errors.Errorf("invalid file path: %s", filePath)
310: 	}
311: 	minorVersion := elements[len(elements)-2]
312: 	rawPatchVersion := strings.Split(elements[len(elements)-1], MigrateFileNameSplit)[0]
313: 	patchVersion, err := strconv.Atoi(rawPatchVersion)
314: 	if err != nil {
315: 		return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to convert patch version to int: %s", rawPatchVersion)
316: 	}
317: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d", minorVersion, patchVersion+1), nil
318: }
319: 
320: // execute runs a single SQL statement within a transaction.
321: func (*Store) execute(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, stmt string) error {
322: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, stmt); err != nil {
323: 		// Tolerate "duplicate column" errors for ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN.
324: 		// This makes migrations idempotent if re-run (e.g., corrupted history).
325: 		errMsg := err.Error()
326: 		if strings.Contains(errMsg, "duplicate column") ||
327: 			strings.Contains(errMsg, "already exists") ||
328: 			strings.Contains(errMsg, "column already exists") {
329: 			slog.Warn("migration: column already exists, skipping", slog.String("error", errMsg))
330: 			return nil
331: 		}
332: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to execute statement")
333: 	}
334: 	return nil
335: }
336: 
337: func (s *Store) normalizedMigrationHistoryList(ctx context.Context) error {
338: 	migrationHistoryList, err := s.driver.FindMigrationHistoryList(ctx, &FindMigrationHistory{})
339: 	if err != nil {
340: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to find migration history")
341: 	}
342: 	versions := []string{}
343: 	for _, migrationHistory := range migrationHistoryList {
344: 		versions = append(versions, migrationHistory.Version)
345: 	}
346: 	sort.Sort(version.SortVersion(versions))
347: 	latestVersion := versions[len(versions)-1]
348: 	latestMinorVersion := version.GetMinorVersion(latestVersion)
349: 
350: 	// If the latest version is greater than 0.22, return.
351: 	// As of 0.22, the migration history is already normalized.
352: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(latestMinorVersion, "0.22") {
353: 		return nil
354: 	}
355: 
356: 	schemaVersionMap := map[string]string{}
357: 	filePaths, err := fs.Glob(MigrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
358: 	if err != nil {
359: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
360: 	}
361: 	sort.Strings(filePaths)
362: 	for _, filePath := range filePaths {
363: 		fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
364: 		if err != nil {
365: 			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
366: 		}
367: 		schemaVersionMap[version.GetMinorVersion(fileSchemaVersion)] = fileSchemaVersion
368: 	}
369: 
370: 	latestSchemaVersion := schemaVersionMap[latestMinorVersion]
371: 	if latestSchemaVersion == "" {
372: 		return errors.Errorf("latest schema version not found")
373: 	}
374: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterOrEqualThan(latestVersion, latestSchemaVersion) {
375: 		return nil
376: 	}
377: 
378: 	// Start a transaction to insert the latest schema version to migration_history.
379: 	tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
380: 	if err != nil {
381: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
382: 	}
383: 	defer tx.Rollback()
384: 	if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO migration_history (version) VALUES ('%s')", latestSchemaVersion)); err != nil {
385: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to insert migration history")
386: 	}
387: 	return tx.Commit()
388: }
389: 
390: func (s *Store) updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx context.Context, schemaVersion string) error {
391: 	workspaceBasicSetting, err := s.GetWorkspaceBasicSetting(ctx)
392: 	if err != nil {
393: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get workspace basic setting")
394: 	}
395: 	workspaceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion = schemaVersion
396: 	if _, err := s.UpsertWorkspaceSetting(ctx, &storepb.WorkspaceSetting{
397: 		Key:   storepb.WorkspaceSettingKey_BASIC,
398: 		Value: &storepb.WorkspaceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: workspaceBasicSetting},
399: 	}); err != nil {
400: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert workspace setting")
401: 	}
402: 	return nil
403: }

12: // isTransientError checks if the error is a transient Postgres error
13: // that may succeed on retry.
14: func isTransientError(err error) bool {
15: 	if err == nil {
16: 		return false
17: 	}
18: 	var pgErr *pgconn.PgError
19: 	if !errors.As(err, &pgErr) {
20: 		return false
21: 	}
22: 	switch pgErr.Code {
23: 	case "57P01": // admin_shutdown
24: 		return true
25: 	case "08006": // connection_failure
26: 		return true
27: 	case "08003": // connection_does_not_exist
28: 		return true
29: 	case "08001": // sqlclient_unable_to_establish_sqlconnection
30: 		return true
31: 	case "08004": // sqlserver_rejected_establishment_of_sqlconnection
32: 		return true
33: 	}
34: 	return false
35: }
36: 
37: // isUniqueViolation checks if the error is a unique constraint violation.
38: func isUniqueViolation(err error) bool {
39: 	if err == nil {
40: 		return false
41: 	}
42: 	var pgErr *pgconn.PgError
43: 	if !errors.As(err, &pgErr) {
44: 		return false
45: 	}
46: 	return pgErr.Code == "23505"
47: }
48: 
49: // RunResiliently executes fn with exponential backoff retry for transient errors.
50: // Unique violations (23505) are treated as success.
51: func RunResiliently(fn func() error) error {
52: 	maxRetries := 5
53: 	backoff := time.Second
54: 
55: 	for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
56: 		err := fn()
57: 		if err == nil {
58: 			return nil
59: 		}
60: 		// Unique violation is treated as success (idempotent insert)
61: 		if isUniqueViolation(err) {
62: 			slog.Warn("unique violation treated as success", "error", err)
63: 			return nil
64: 		}
65: 		// Non-transient error: fail immediately
66: 		if !isTransientError(err) {
67: 			return err
68: 		}
69: 		// Transient error: retry with backoff
70: 		if attempt == maxRetries {
71: 			return err
72: 		}
73: 		jitter := time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(backoff) / 2))
74: 		sleepDuration := backoff + jitter
75: 		slog.Warn("transient error, retrying",
76: 			"error", err,
77: 			"attempt", attempt+1,
78: 			"maxRetries", maxRetries,
79: 			"sleep", sleepDuration,
80: 		)
81: 		time.Sleep(sleepDuration)
82: 		backoff *= 2
83: 	}
84: 	return errors.New("max retries exceeded")
85: }

package postgres

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
)

var (
	protojsonUnmarshaler = protojson.UnmarshalOptions{
		DiscardUnknown: true,
	}
)

func placeholder(n int) string {
	return "$" + fmt.Sprint(n)
}

func placeholders(n int) string {
	list := []string{}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		list = append(list, placeholder(i+1))
	}
	return strings.Join(list, ", ")
}

# Docs > Stable > SERIAL
## Modes of operation

The keyword `SERIAL` is recognized in `CREATE TABLE` and is automatically translated to a real data type and a [`DEFAULT` expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/default-value) during table creation. The result of this translation is then used internally by CockroachDB, and can be observed using [`SHOW CREATE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/show-create).

The chosen `DEFAULT` expression ensures that different values are automatically generated for the column during row insertion. These are not guaranteed to increase monotonically, see [this section below](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/serial#auto-incrementing-is-not-always-sequential) for details.

There are five possible translation modes for `SERIAL`:
| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `rowid` (default) | `SERIAL` implies `DEFAULT unique_rowid()`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/set-vars) or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cluster-settings). |
| `unordered_rowid` | `SERIAL` implies `DEFAULT unordered_unique_rowid()`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/set-vars) or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cluster-settings). |
| `virtual_sequence` | `SERIAL` creates a virtual sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` session variable or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` cluster setting. |
| `sql_sequence` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. |
| `sql_sequence_cached` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`, caching the results for reuse in the current session. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. When the cache is empty, the underlying sequence will only be incremented once to populate the cache.When this mode is set, the `sql.defaults.serial_sequences_cache_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cluster-settings) controls the number of values to cache in a user's session, with a default of 256. |

These modes can be configured with the [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/set-vars) `serial_normalization`.

Note:
The particular choice of `DEFAULT` expression when clients use the `SERIAL` keyword is subject to change in future versions of CockroachDB. Applications that wish to use `unique_rowid()` specifically must use the full explicit syntax `INT DEFAULT unique_rowid()` and avoid `SERIAL` altogether.

Note:
Use [`ALTER ROLE ALL SET {sessionvar} = {val}`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/alter-role#set-default-session-variable-values-for-all-users) instead of the `sql.defaults.*` [cluster settings](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cluster-settings). This allows you to set a default value for all users for any [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/set-vars) that applies during login, making the `sql.defaults.*` cluster settings redundant.

The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/set-vars) or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/cluster-settings). |
| `unordered_rowid` | `SERIAL` implies `DEFAULT unordered_unique_rowid()`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/set-vars) or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/cluster-settings). |
| `virtual_sequence` | `SERIAL` creates a virtual sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` session variable or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` cluster setting. |
| `sql_sequence` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. |
| `sql_sequence_cached` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`, caching the results for reuse in the current session. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. When the cache is empty, the underlying sequence will only be incremented once to populate the cache.When this mode is set, the `sql.defaults.serial_sequences_cache_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/cluster-settings) controls the number of values to cache in a user's session, with a default of 256. |

These modes can be configured with the [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/set-vars) `serial_normalization`.

Note:

Note:
Use [`ALTER ROLE ALL SET {sessionvar} = {val}`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/alter-role#set-default-session-variable-values-for-all-users) instead of the `sql.defaults.*` [cluster settings](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/cluster-settings). This allows you to set a default value for all users for any [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/set-vars) that applies during login, making the `sql.defaults.*` cluster settings redundant.

# Docs > V25.2 > SERIAL
## Modes of operation

The keyword `SERIAL` is recognized in `CREATE TABLE` and is automatically translated to a real data type and a [`DEFAULT` expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/default-value) during table creation. The result of this translation is then used internally by CockroachDB, and can be observed using [`SHOW CREATE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/show-create).

The chosen `DEFAULT` expression ensures that different values are automatically generated for the column during row insertion. These are not guaranteed to increase monotonically, see [this section below](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/serial#auto-incrementing-is-not-always-sequential) for details.

| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `rowid` (default) | `SERIAL` implies `DEFAULT unique_rowid()`. The real data type is always `INT8`, regardless of the `default_int_size` [session variable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/set-vars) or `sql.defaults.default_int_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/cluster-settings). |
| `unordered_rowid` | `SERIAL` implies `DEFAULT unordered_unique_rowid()`. | `sql_sequence` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. |
| `sql_sequence_cached` | `SERIAL` creates a regular SQL sequence and implies `DEFAULT nextval(<seqname>)`, caching the results for reuse in the current session. The real data type depends on `SERIAL` variant. When the cache is empty, the underlying sequence will only be incremented once to populate the cache.When this mode is set, the `sql.defaults.serial_sequences_cache_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/cluster-settings) controls the number of values to cache in a user's session, with a default of 256. |

Note:
Use [`ALTER ROLE ALL SET {sessionvar} = {val}`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/alter-role#set-default-session-variable-values-for-all-users) instead of the `sql.defaults.*` [cluster settings](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.2/cluster-settings). **Tool: cockroachdb_search_cockroach_db_knowledge_sources**

**Input:**
```json
{
  "query": "What are the limitations of performing schema changes or DDL statements inside an explicit transaction in CockroachDB?"
}
```

**Output:**
```
# Docs > Stable > Online Schema Changes > Known limitations
## Schema changes within transactions

Most schema changes should not be performed within an explicit transaction with multiple statements, as they do not have the same atomicity guarantees as other SQL statements. Execute schema changes either as single statements (as an implicit transaction), or in an explicit transaction consisting of the single schema change statement. There are some exceptions to this, detailed below.

Schema changes keep your data consistent at all times, but they do not run inside [transactions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/transactions) in the general case. Making schema changes transactional would mean requiring a given schema change to propagate across all the nodes of a cluster. This would block all user-initiated transactions being run by your application, since the schema change would have to commit before any other transactions could make progress. This would prevent the cluster from servicing reads and writes during the schema change, requiring application downtime.

Tip:
Some tools and applications may be able to workaround CockroachDB's lack of transactional schema changes by [enabling a setting that automatically commits before running schema changes inside transactions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/online-schema-changes#enable-automatic-commit-before-running-schema-changes-inside-transactions).

Some schema change operations can be run within explicit, multiple statement transactions. `CREATE TABLE` and `CREATE INDEX` statements can be run within the same transaction with the same atomicity guarantees as other SQL statements. There are no performance or rollback issues when using these statements within a multiple statement transaction.

Within a single [transaction](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/transactions):

- You can run schema changes inside the same transaction as a [`CREATE TABLE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/create-table) statement. For more information, see [Run schema changes inside a transaction with `CREATE TABLE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/online-schema-changes#run-schema-changes-inside-a-transaction-with-create-table). However, a `CREATE TABLE` statement containing [`FOREIGN KEY`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/foreign-key) clauses cannot be followed by statements that reference the new table.
- [Schema change DDL statements inside a multi-statement transaction can fail while other statements succeed](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/online-schema-changes#schema-change-ddl-statements-inside-a-multi-statement-transaction-can-fail-while-other-statements-succeed).
- [`DROP COLUMN`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/alter-table#drop-column) can result in data loss if one of the other schema changes in the transaction fails or is canceled. To work around this, move the `DROP COLUMN` statement to its own explicit transaction or run it in a single statement outside the existing transaction.

Note:
If a schema change within a transaction fails, manual intervention may be needed to determine which statement has failed. After determining which schema change(s) failed, you can then retry the schema change.
