# Github Issue (closed): pkg/ccl/logictestccl/tests/local-repeatable-read/local-repeatable-read_test: TestRepeatableReadLogic_select_for_share failed
## Comments

4. **root&#x27;s `SELECT * FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`** encounters:
   - **Key 1:** testuser holds a shared replicated lock → correctly skipped
   - **Key 2:** unresolved intent from the already-committed INSERT → **incorrectly skipped**

5. The MVCC scanner at [pebble_mvcc_scanner.go:1003-1015](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0cb591927ad6b9b2d547d71552716c5515618cec/pkg/storage/pebble_mvcc_scanner.go#L1003-L1015) treats **all** intents from other transactions as &quot;locked&quot; when `skipLocked` is set. It does not check whether the intent&#x27;s transaction has already committed or aborted:
   ```go
   if p.skipLocked {
       // 10. The scanner has been configured with the skipLocked option. Ignore
       // intents written by other transactions and seek to the next key.
       ...
       return true /* ok */, false
   }
   ```

6. The concurrency manager intentionally **skips lock table scanning** for SKIP LOCKED requests ([lock_table.go:4556-4561](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0cb591927ad6b9b2d547d71552716c5515618cec/pkg/kv/kvserver/concurrency/lock_table.go#L4556-L4561)), so there is no upfront intent resolution. And intent resolution after the SKIP LOCKED scan is async/best-effort ([replica_read.go:315-316](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0cb591927ad6b9b2d547d71552716c5515618cec/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_read.go#L315-L316)).

This is a **real correctness bug** in the SKIP LOCKED implementation: stale intents from committed transactions can cause SKIP LOCKED to incorrectly skip rows that are not actually locked. The metamorphic `max-intents-in-flight-per-caller = 1` setting widens the race window significantly, making this flake reproducible.

**Potential fix direction:** The MVCC scanner could resolve (or check the status of) the intent&#x27;s transaction before deciding to skip the key. Alternatively, the SKIP LOCKED path could be changed to perform synchronous intent resolution for encountered intents rather than treating them as locks.

**Related Issues and PRs**

- **#167370** — Same test, same failure, closed as rare flake (2 days before this issue). Same failure mode confirmed.
- **#121917** — `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED skips unlocked rows sometimes?` — Open issue reporting similar user-visible behavior in production workloads. While that issue discusses optimizer plan bugs as well, the underlying MVCC intent-skipping problem described here is also a contributing factor.
- **#129921** — Prior flake investigations on `select_for_share` test.
- **bac5c82b0a5** — `kv: correctly handle replicated locks when using the SKIP LOCKED policy` — Added the test section that is now failing, but did not address the stale-intent skipping problem.
- **2c1e0c0b3ca** — `logictest: fix another flake in select_for_share` — Fixed a different flake in the same test (unexpected lock in `cluster_locks`), not this one.

**Timeline**

- **2024-01-17:** Commit bac5c82b0a5 introduced the test section (lines 209–251) as part of adding replicated lock support to SKIP LOCKED.
- **2026-04-03:** First failure in #167370, SHA `f664d721208` — same error, `max-intents-in-flight-per-caller = 1`.
- **2026-04-03:** #167370 closed as rare flake.
- **2026-04-04:** Second failure in #167458, SHA `0cb591927ad` — same error, `max-intents-in-flight-per-caller = 1`. Reopened as a new issue with release-blocker label.
- **2026-04-05:** @stevendanna posted a detailed root cause analysis confirming the mechanism.

&lt;details&gt;
&lt;summary&gt;Detailed evidence and investigation notes&lt;/summary&gt;

**Log Excerpts**

From `test.log` (shard 10, run 10):

```
metamorphic: use COCKROACH_RANDOM_SEED=-4330465129718265628 for reproduction
initialized metamorphic constant &quot;max-intents-in-flight-per-caller&quot; with value 1
...
logic.go:3277:
     select_for_share:234: BEGIN;
     SELECT * FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
     expected:
         2

     but found (query options: &quot;&quot;) :

```

# Github Issue (open): pkg/sql/logictest/tests/local-repeatable-read/local-repeatable-read_test: TestLogic_select_for_share failed
## Comments

**Comment by COLLABORATOR (0 upvotes, 0 downvotes)**:
/investigate

**Comment by CONTRIBUTOR (0 upvotes, 0 downvotes)**:
**Investigation: TestLogic_select_for_share (local-repeatable-read)**

**Investigated failure:** [#170697](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/170697)
**Failure SHA:** `f4de542b4e2d0a3074d9590a220500c1dd211caa`
**Confidence:** high

**What This Test Does**

The `select_for_share` logic test validates shared and exclusive lock acquisition behavior under `SELECT ... FOR SHARE` and `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, including interactions with the `SKIP LOCKED` wait policy. The failing section (lines 209-269) tests that `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and `FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED` correctly skip only keys that are actually locked by other transactions when using replicated (durable) locks.

**Where the Failure Occurs**

The test fails at [select_for_share:242](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f4de542b4e2d0a3074d9590a220500c1dd211caa/pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/select_for_share#L242) in the `local-repeatable-read` config:

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
```

Expected result: `2` (key 2 should be returned since only key 1 is locked by a shared lock from another transaction).
Actual result: empty (both keys were skipped).

**Analysis**

**Hypothesis: SKIP LOCKED skips key with unresolved INSERT intent due to VIR + serialized intent resolution**
Confidence: **high**

Three metamorphic constants combine to trigger this failure (from `test.log`):

1. `kv.concurrency.virtual_intent_resolution.enabled = true` (line 35)
2. `max-intents-in-flight-per-caller = 1` (line 13)
3. `kv.transaction.write_buffering.enabled = false` (line 16)

The test scenario:

1. **Line 214**: `INSERT INTO t VALUES(1), (2)` writes MVCC intents on keys 1 and 2.
2. **Line 219-223**: `SELECT * FROM t` (a non-locking read) is intended to force intent resolution before SKIP LOCKED scans. This was the fix from [3371b8c](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/commit/3371b8c3285158c2f51481e997e2c1d65a24a1dc) for #167458.
3. **However**, with VIR enabled, non-locking reads [virtually resolve intents](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f4de542b4e2d0a3074d9590a220500c1dd211caa/pkg/kv/kvserver/concurrency/concurrency_manager.go#L870-L881) in an in-memory batch without physically removing them from MVCC storage. The read succeeds, but the INSERT intents remain on disk.
4. Physical intent resolution is delegated to an async path, but with `max-intents-in-flight-per-caller=1`, resolution is serialized and may be delayed.
5. **Line 230-234**: `testuser` runs `SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = 1 FOR SHARE` — this is a **locking** read, so VIR does not apply. The INSERT intent on key 1 is physically resolved, and a new replicated shared lock (intent) is acquired on key 1. Key 2&#x27;s INSERT intent is **not** touched by this point query.
6. **Line 242-244**: `root` runs `SELECT * FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. The MVCC scanner encounters:
   - Key 1: intent from testuser&#x27;s active FOR SHARE transaction → correctly skipped (lock conflict)
   - Key 2: **still-unresolved INSERT intent** from the committed INSERT transaction → [unconditionally skipped by SKIP LOCKED](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f4de542b4e2d0a3074d9590a220500c1dd211caa/pkg/storage/pebble_mvcc_scanner.go#L1003-L1015) without checking transaction status

Result: empty set instead of `{2}`.

This is a manifestation of the known bug **#167582** (&quot;SKIP LOCKED skips keys with intents from committed transactions&quot;). The MVCC scanner&#x27;s SKIP LOCKED path at [pebble_mvcc_scanner.go:1003-1015](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f4de542b4e2d0a3074d9590a220500c1dd211caa/pkg/storage/pebble_mvcc_scanner.go#L1003-L1015) unconditionally skips keys with intents from other transactions without checking the intent&#x27;s transaction status.

# Docs > Stable
## FOR UPDATE and FOR SHARE

`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and `SELECT ... FOR SHARE` are used to issue [locking reads](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/read-committed#locking-reads) at different [lock strengths](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/select-for-update#lock-strengths).

### Syntax

FOR

NO

KEY

UPDATE

KEY

SHARE

OFtable_name_list

SKIP

LOCKED

NOWAIT

Tip:
For the full `SELECT` statement syntax documentation, see [Selection Queries](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/selection-queries).

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `FOR SHARE` | Acquire a shared lock on the rows returned by the [`SELECT`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/selection-queries) statement. Shared locks are not enabled by default for `SERIALIZABLE` transactions. For details, see [`FOR SHARE` usage](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/select-for-update#for-share-usage). |
| `FOR UPDATE` | Acquire an exclusive lock on the rows returned by the [`SELECT`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/selection-queries) statement. For details, see [`FOR UPDATE` usage](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/select-for-update#for-update-usage). |
Under `SERIALIZABLE` isolation:

- Shared locks are not enabled by default. To enable shared locks for `SERIALIZABLE` transactions, configure the [`enable_shared_locking_for_serializable` session setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/session-variables). To perform [foreign key](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/foreign-key) checks under `SERIALIZABLE` isolation with shared locks, configure the [`enable_implicit_fk_locking_for_serializable` session setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/session-variables). This matches the default [`READ COMMITTED`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/read-committed) behavior.
- If the [`optimizer_use_lock_op_for_serializable` session setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/session-variables) is enabled, the [cost-based optimizer](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cost-based-optimizer) uses a `Lock` operator to construct query plans for `SELECT` statements using the `FOR UPDATE` and `FOR SHARE` clauses. This more closely matches the PostgreSQL behavior, but will create more round trips from [gateway node](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/architecture/sql-layer#gateway-node) to [replica leaseholder](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/architecture/replication-layer#leases) in some cases.

#### Lock strengths

Lock "strength" determines how restrictive the lock is to concurrent transactions attempting to access the same row.

- `SELECT FOR UPDATE` obtains an *exclusive lock* on each qualifying row, blocking concurrent writes and locking reads on the row. Only one transaction can hold an exclusive lock on a row at a time, and only the transaction holding the exclusive lock can write to the row.
- `SELECT FOR SHARE` obtains a *shared lock* on each qualifying row, blocking concurrent writes and **exclusive** locking reads on the row. Multiple transactions can hold a shared lock on a row at the same time. When multiple transactions hold a shared lock on a row, none can write to the row. A shared lock grants transactions mutual read-only access to a row, and ensures that they read the latest version of the row.

When a `SELECT FOR UPDATE` or `SELECT FOR SHARE` read is issued on a row, only the latest version of the row is returned to the client. Under [`READ COMMITTED`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/read-committed) isolation, neither statement will block concurrent, non-locking reads.

Note that CockroachDB [ensures serializability](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/demo-serializable) when using `SERIALIZABLE` isolation, regardless of the specified lock strength.
```

# Docs > V23.2 > Session Variables
## Supported variables

| Variable name | Description | Initial value | Modify with [`SET`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/set-vars)? | View with [`SHOW`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/show-vars)? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `serial_normalization` | Specifies the default handling of [`SERIAL`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/serial) in table definitions. Valid options include `'rowid'`, `'virtual_sequence'`, `sql_sequence`, `sql_sequence_cached`, and `unordered_rowid`. If set to `'virtual_sequence'`, the `SERIAL` type auto-creates a sequence for [better compatibility with Hibernate sequences](https://forum.cockroachlabs.com/t/hibernate-sequence-generator-returns-negative-number-and-ignore-unique-rowid/1885). If set to `sql_sequence_cached`, you can use the `sql.defaults.serial_sequences_cache_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cluster-settings) to control the number of values to cache in a user's session, with a default of 256. If set to `unordered_rowid`, the `SERIAL` type generates a globally unique 64-bit integer (a combination of the insert timestamp and the ID of the node executing the statement) that does not have unique ordering. | `'rowid'` | Yes | Yes |
| `server_version` | The version of PostgreSQL that CockroachDB emulates. | Version-dependent | No | Yes |
| `server_version_num` | The version of PostgreSQL that CockroachDB emulates. | Version-dependent | Yes | Yes |
| `session_id` | The ID of the current session. | Session-dependent | No | Yes |
| `session_user` | The user connected for the current session. | User in connection string | No | Yes |
| `sql_safe_updates` | If `false`, potentially unsafe SQL statements are allowed, including `DROP` of a non-empty database and all dependent objects, [`DELETE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/delete) without a `WHERE` clause, [`UPDATE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/update) without a `WHERE` clause, and [`ALTER TABLE .. DROP COLUMN`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/alter-table#drop-column). See [Allow Potentially Unsafe SQL Statements](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cockroach-sql#allow-potentially-unsafe-sql-statements) for more details. | `true` for interactive sessions from the [built-in SQL client](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cockroach-sql), `false` for sessions from other clients | Yes | Yes |
| `statement_timeout` | The amount of time a statement can run before being stopped. This value can be an `int` (e.g., `10`) and will be interpreted as milliseconds. It can also be an interval or string argument, where the string can be parsed as a valid interval (e.g., `'4s'`). A value of `0` turns it off. | The value set by the `sql.defaults.statement_timeout` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cluster-settings) (`0s`, by default). | Yes | Yes |
| `stub_catalog_tables` | If `off`, querying an unimplemented, empty [`pg_catalog`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/pg-catalog) table will result in an error, as is the case in v20.2 and earlier. If `on`, querying an unimplemented, empty `pg_catalog` table simply returns no rows. | `on` | Yes | Yes |
| `timezone` | The default time zone for the current session. This session variable was named `"time zone"` (with a space) in CockroachDB 1.x. It has been renamed for compatibility with PostgreSQL. | `UTC` | Yes | Yes |
| `tracing` | The trace recording state. | `off` |  | Yes |
| `transaction_isolation` | The isolation level at which the transaction executes ([`SERIALIZABLE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/demo-serializable) or [`READ COMMITTED`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/read-committed)). See [Isolation levels](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/transactions#isolation-levels). | `SERIALIZABLE` | Yes | Yes |

| `serial_normalization` | Specifies the default handling of [`SERIAL`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/serial) in table definitions. Valid options include `'rowid'`, `'virtual_sequence'`, `sql_sequence`, `sql_sequence_cached`, and `unordered_rowid`. If set to `'virtual_sequence'`, the `SERIAL` type auto-creates a sequence for [better compatibility with Hibernate sequences](https://forum.cockroachlabs.com/t/hibernate-sequence-generator-returns-negative-number-and-ignore-unique-rowid/1885). If set to `sql_sequence_cached`, you can use the `sql.defaults.serial_sequences_cache_size` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cluster-settings) to control the number of values to cache in a user's session, with a default of 256. If set to `unordered_rowid`, the `SERIAL` type generates a globally unique 64-bit integer (a combination of the insert timestamp and the ID of the node executing the statement) that does not have unique ordering. | `'rowid'` | Yes | Yes |
| `server_version` | The version of PostgreSQL that CockroachDB emulates. | Version-dependent | No | Yes |
| `server_version_num` | The version of PostgreSQL that CockroachDB emulates. | Version-dependent | Yes | Yes |
| `session_id` | The ID of the current session. | Session-dependent | No | Yes |
| `session_user` | The user connected for the current session. | User in connection string | No | Yes |
| `sql_safe_updates` | If `false`, potentially unsafe SQL statements are allowed, including `DROP` of a non-empty database and all dependent objects, [`DELETE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/delete) without a `WHERE` clause, [`UPDATE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/update) without a `WHERE` clause, and [`ALTER TABLE .. DROP COLUMN`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/alter-table#drop-column). See [Allow Potentially Unsafe SQL Statements](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cockroach-sql#allow-potentially-unsafe-sql-statements) for more details. | `true` for interactive sessions from the [built-in SQL client](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cockroach-sql), `false` for sessions from other clients | Yes | Yes |
| `statement_timeout` | The amount of time a statement can run before being stopped. This value can be an `int` (e.g., `10`) and will be interpreted as milliseconds. It can also be an interval or string argument, where the string can be parsed as a valid interval (e.g., `'4s'`). A value of `0` turns it off. | The value set by the `sql.defaults.statement_timeout` [cluster setting](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cluster-settings) (`0s`, by default). | Yes | Yes |
| `stub_catalog_tables` | If `off`, querying an unimplemented, empty [`pg_catalog`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/pg-catalog) table will result in an error, as is the case in v20.2 and earlier. If `on`, querying an unimplemented, empty `pg_catalog` table simply returns no rows. | `on` | Yes | Yes |
| `timezone` | The default time zone for the current session. This session variable was named `"time zone"` (with a space) in CockroachDB 1.x. It has been renamed for compatibility with PostgreSQL. | `UTC` | Yes | Yes |
| `tracing` | The trace recording state. | `off` |  | Yes |
| `transaction_isolation` | The isolation level at which the transaction executes ([`SERIALIZABLE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/demo-serializable) or [`READ COMMITTED`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/read-committed)). See [Isolation levels](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/transactions#isolation-levels). | `SERIALIZABLE` | Yes | Yes |

228: 
229: 	// Sort seed files by name. This is important to ensure that seed files are applied in order.
230: 	sort.Strings(filenames)
231: 	// Start a transaction to apply the seed files.
232: 	tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
233: 	if err != nil {
234: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
235: 	}
236: 	defer tx.Rollback()
237: 	// Loop over all seed files and execute them in order.
238: 	for _, filename := range filenames {
239: 		bytes, err := seedFS.ReadFile(filename)
240: 		if err != nil {
241: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read seed file, filename=%s", filename)
242: 		}
243: 		if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
244: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "seed error: %s", filename)
245: 		}
246: 	}
247: 	return tx.Commit()
248: }

250: // GetCurrentSchemaVersion scans ALL migration subdirectories in the embedded FS
251: // to find the highest version file. The filesystem is the single source of truth.
252: //
253: // NOTE: This function does NOT call itself recursively. The */*.sql glob does NOT
254: // match LATEST.sql (which sits at the base path, not inside a subdirectory).
255: // getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript() calls GetCurrentSchemaVersion() when it
256: // encounters LATEST.sql, but that path is never reached from this glob.
257: func (s *Store) GetCurrentSchemaVersion() (string, error) {
258: 	filePaths, err := fs.Glob(MigrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
259: 	if err != nil {
260: 		return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to glob migration files")
261: 	}
262: 	if len(filePaths) == 0 {
263: 		return "", errors.Errorf("no migration files found in %s", s.getMigrationBasePath())
264: 	}
265: 	sort.Strings(filePaths) // fs.Glob does not guarantee sorted order
266: 
267: 	var maxVersion string
268: 	for _, filePath := range filePaths {
269: 		fileVer, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
270: 		if err != nil {
271: 			continue // skip files that can't be parsed (e.g., LATEST.sql at base path)
272: 		}
273: 		if maxVersion == "" || version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileVer, maxVersion) {
274: 			maxVersion = fileVer
275: 		}
276: 	}
277: 	if maxVersion == "" {
278: 		return "", errors.Errorf("could not determine schema version from migration files")
279: 	}
280: 	return maxVersion, nil
281: }
282: 
283: func (s *Store) validateSchemaVersionConsistency() error {
284: 	fsVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
285: 	if err != nil {
286: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get FS schema version")
287: 	}
288: 	codeVersion := version.GetCurrentVersion(s.profile.Mode)
289: 	codeMinor := version.GetMinorVersion(codeVersion)
290: 	fsMinor := version.GetMinorVersion(fsVersion)
291: 
292: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fsMinor, codeMinor) {
293: 		slog.Warn("migration FS has directories newer than code version; bump Version/DevVersion",
294: 			"fs_minor", fsMinor, "code_minor", codeMinor,
295: 			"fs_version", fsVersion, "code_version", codeVersion)
296: 	}
297: 	return nil // warn-only at runtime; build-time gate catches this earlier
298: }
299: 
300: func (s *Store) getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath string) (string, error) {
301: 	// If the file is the latest schema file, return the current schema version.
302: 	if strings.HasSuffix(filePath, LatestSchemaFileName) {
303: 		return s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
304: 	}
305: 
306: 	normalizedPath := filepath.ToSlash(filePath)
307: 	elements := strings.Split(normalizedPath, "/")
308: 	if len(elements) < 2 {
309: 		return "", errors.Errorf("invalid file path: %s", filePath)
310: 	}
311: 	minorVersion := elements[len(elements)-2]
312: 	rawPatchVersion := strings.Split(elements[len(elements)-1], MigrateFileNameSplit)[0]
313: 	patchVersion, err := strconv.Atoi(rawPatchVersion)
314: 	if err != nil {
315: 		return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to convert patch version to int: %s", rawPatchVersion)
316: 	}
317: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d", minorVersion, patchVersion+1), nil
318: }
319: 
320: // execute runs a single SQL statement within a transaction.
321: func (*Store) execute(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, stmt string) error {
322: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, stmt); err != nil {
323: 		// Tolerate "duplicate column" errors for ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN.
324: 		// This makes migrations idempotent if re-run (e.g., corrupted history).
325: 		errMsg := err.Error()
326: 		if strings.Contains(errMsg, "duplicate column") ||
327: 			strings.Contains(errMsg, "already exists") ||
328: 			strings.Contains(errMsg, "column already exists") {
329: 			slog.Warn("migration: column already exists, skipping", slog.String("error", errMsg))
330: 			return nil
331: 		}
332: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to execute statement")
333: 	}
334: 	return nil
335: }
336: 
337: func (s *Store) normalizedMigrationHistoryList(ctx context.Context) error {
338: 	migrationHistoryList, err := s.driver.FindMigrationHistoryList(ctx, &FindMigrationHistory{})
339: 	if err != nil {
340: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to find migration history")
341: 	}
342: 	versions := []string{}
343: 	for _, migrationHistory := range migrationHistoryList {
344: 		versions = append(versions, migrationHistory.Version)
345: 	}
346: 	sort.Sort(version.SortVersion(versions))
347: 	latestVersion := versions[len(versions)-1]
348: 	latestMinorVersion := version.GetMinorVersion(latestVersion)
349: 
350: 	// If the latest version is greater than 0.22, return.
351: 	// As of 0.22, the migration history is already normalized.
352: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(latestMinorVersion, "0.22") {
353: 		return nil
354: 	}
355: 
356: 	schemaVersionMap := map[string]string{}
357: 	filePaths, err := fs.Glob(MigrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
358: 	if err != nil {
359: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
360: 	}
361: 	sort.Strings(filePaths)
362: 	for _, filePath := range filePaths {
363: 		fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
364: 		if err != nil {
365: 			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
366: 		}
367: 		schemaVersionMap[version.GetMinorVersion(fileSchemaVersion)] = fileSchemaVersion
368: 	}
369: 
370: 	latestSchemaVersion := schemaVersionMap[latestMinorVersion]
371: 	if latestSchemaVersion == "" {
372: 		return errors.Errorf("latest schema version not found")
373: 	}
374: 	if version.IsVersionGreaterOrEqualThan(latestVersion, latestSchemaVersion) {
375: 		return nil
376: 	}
377: 
378: 	// Start a transaction to insert the latest schema version to migration_history.
379: 	tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
380: 	if err != nil {
381: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
382: 	}
383: 	defer tx.Rollback()
384: 	if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO migration_history (version) VALUES ('%s')", latestSchemaVersion)); err != nil {
385: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to insert migration history")
386: 	}
387: 	return tx.Commit()
388: }
389: 
390: func (s *Store) updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx context.Context, schemaVersion string) error {
391: 	workspaceBasicSetting, err := s.GetWorkspaceBasicSetting(ctx)
392: 	if err != nil {
393: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get workspace basic setting")
394: 	}
395: 	workspaceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion = schemaVersion
396: 	if _, err := s.UpsertWorkspaceSetting(ctx, &storepb.WorkspaceSetting{
397: 		Key:   storepb.WorkspaceSettingKey_BASIC,
398: 		Value: &storepb.WorkspaceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: workspaceBasicSetting},
399: 	}); err != nil {
400: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert workspace setting")
401: 	}
402: 	return nil

func (d *DB) createBridgeHandoffAttempt(ctx context.Context, tenantID int32, sessionID string, now time.Time) (*store.BridgeHandoff, error) {
	tx, err := d.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("begin bridge handoff transaction: %w", err)
	}
	defer tx.Rollback()

	var externalSessionID int64
	err = tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
		UPDATE bridge_external_sessions
		SET updated_at = updated_at
		WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND session_id = $2
		RETURNING id
	`, tenantID, sessionID).Scan(&externalSessionID)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		return nil, store.ErrBridgeExternalSessionNotFound
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("lock bridge external session: %w", err)
	}

	var activeCount int
	if err := tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, `SELECT COUNT(1) FROM bridge_handoffs WHERE external_session_id = $1 AND active = true`, externalSessionID).Scan(&activeCount); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("check active bridge handoff: %w", err)
	}
	if activeCount != 0 {
		return nil, store.ErrBridgeHandoffConflict
	}

	var generation int
	if err := tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(generation), 0) + 1 FROM bridge_handoffs WHERE external_session_id = $1`, externalSessionID).Scan(&generation); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("allocate bridge handoff generation: %w", err)
	}

	handoffID := uuid.NewString()
	var id int64
	err = tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
		INSERT INTO bridge_handoffs (
			external_session_id, handoff_id, tenant_id, session_id, generation,
			routing_mode, outcome, active, version, created_at, updated_at
		) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, 'handoff_queued', NULL, true, 1, $6, $7)
		RETURNING id
	`, externalSessionID, handoffID, tenantID, sessionID, generation, now.Unix(), now.Unix()).Scan(&id)
	if err != nil {
		if isPostgresConstraint(err) {
			return nil, store.ErrBridgeHandoffConflict
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("insert bridge handoff: %w", err)
	}
	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit bridge handoff: %w", err)
	}
	return d.findBridgeHandoffByIdentity(ctx, tenantID, sessionID, generation, handoffID)
}

func isPostgresConstraint(err error) bool {
	message := err.Error()
	return containsAny(message,
		"unique_constraint", "foreign_key_constraint", "check_constraint",
		"violates unique constraint", "violates foreign key constraint",
		"violates check constraint", "duplicate key value violates",
	)
}

func isPostgresRetryable(err error) bool {
	message := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
	return strings.Contains(message, "deadlock") || strings.Contains(message, "lock not available") || strings.Contains(message, "could not serialize")
}

func containsAny(s string, substrs ...string) bool {
	for _, substr := range substrs {
		if strings.Contains(s, substr) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (d *DB) CreateAgentMessages(ctx context.Context, messages []*store.AgentMessageRecord) error {
	if len(messages) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	tx, err := d.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback()

	stmt := `
		INSERT INTO agent_messages (session_id, tenant_id, source, source_id, role, content, created_at)
		VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)
	`
	for _, m := range messages {
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, stmt, m.SessionID, m.TenantID, m.Source, m.SourceID, m.Role, m.Content, m.CreatedAt); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return tx.Commit()
}

		}

	return &m, nil

## Agreed plan summary (all decisions confirmed)

**Architecture**: single shared implementation — `postgres.NewCockroachDB()` in the existing postgres package, selected via `--driver=cockroach` + `COCKROACH_DSN` (no fallback to `DATABASE_URL`).

**Migrations** (`store/migration/cockroach/`, versioned dirs 0.19–0.35 mirroring postgres + `LATEST.sql`):
- No SQL splitter — keep whole-file `ExecContext` on one connection
- Cockroach path skips `db.Begin()` (DDL doesn't run in explicit tx; `autocommit_before_ddl` dissolves it anyway)
- Migrator injects `SET serial_normalization = 'sql_sequence';` as first statement (session var, MCP-verified; required — `'rowid'` mode overflows Go int32 IDs)
- Atomicity loss documented + mitigated by existing safety net (history-after-success, `IF NOT EXISTS`/`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, duplicate-column tolerance at migrator.go:326)
- PoC gate: `SHOW CREATE TABLE` proving `nextval()` defaults

**Runtime**:
- `simple_protocol` everywhere (parity with postgres.go)
- `crdb.ExecuteTx` retry wrapper (40001) around the 8 tx sites — all audited pure-DB, no side effects inside closures (review Issue 6 ✓); `ClaimPendingEvents` (agent.go:2781) is single-statement, no wrapper needed; SKIP LOCKED supported (v22.2+ docs ✓)
- `bridge.go:320 isPostgresRetryable` string-match hack superseded by pgcode-based retry for cockroach

**plan3.md will include**: capability matrix (review's biggest ask), SQL portability audit, the adversarial pass (every behavioral change answers: PG behavior changed / why CRDB requires it / new failure modes), retry inventory, parity-script extension (validate-parity.sh currently sqlite↔postgres only), vector-table runtime-creation justification, PoC checklist, CI steps.

- serial_normalization is session variable (SET/SHOW), options rowid/virtual_sequence/sql_sequence/sql_sequence_cached/unordered_rowid (+sql_sequence_cached_node v24.1+), default 'rowid' — Session Variables / SET docs
- SKIP LOCKED supported wait policy (stable v26.2 docs + v23.2+); blog statement "doesn't currently support" is outdated
- Known upstream bug #167582: SKIP LOCKED may skip keys with intents from committed transactions (GitHub issue via MCP)
- SELECT FOR SHARE = FOR UPDATE no-op for compat (serializable)
- FOR UPDATE leads to increased throughput; still need app-level retry handling for 40001
- DDL not supported in explicit transactions (mostly); CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX can run in multi-statement transactions; autocommit_before_ddl commits before DDL
- Simple protocol multi-statement batches → automatic retries possible
- extract(epoch from timestamp) → float in CRDB
- Connection pool: active connections across pools ~4× vCPUs
- Vector index limitations: no large batch inserts, no IMPORT INTO, prefix filters only
- pgx integration: simple protocol recommended (pgx.md in bugs/057)
- Docker single-node: COCKROACH_DATABASE/USER/PASSWORD env vars, init scripts

INFERENCES:
- int32 overflow with rowid mode → sql_sequence required
- Whole-file batch = SET applies to subsequent CREATE TABLEs (same connection, session var)
- crdb.ExecuteTx replaces isPostgresRetryable string hack
- etc.

## Assistant (Build · DeepSeek V4 Flash Free (New) · 19.5s)

_Thinking:_

Confirmed via MCP: `extract(..., timestamp) → float` in all stable versions. So `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())` returns float in CRDB. The postgres files use it as DEFAULT for BIGINT columns without explicit cast (19 occurrences). In PostgreSQL, numeric→bigint works via assignment cast in defaults. In CockroachDB, float→int requires an explicit cast (CRDB does not implicitly cast float to int). So the cockroach SQL files MUST add `::BIGINT` (or `::INT8`) — this is a documented portability difference and a concrete action item.

Also runtime: `store/db/postgres/migration_history.go:39` — INSERT INTO migration_history (version, created_ts) VALUES ($1, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())) — need to check the exact query. _Thinking:_

Transaction retry design (review Issue 6)\n\n### 9.1 Inventory of explicit transactions\n\n| # | Site | Function | Transaction body | External side effects inside tx? |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `bridge.go:112` | `createBridgeHandoffAttempt` | UPDATE lock, COUNT, MAX+1, INSERT; post-commit read | none |\n| 2 | `bridge.go:356` | `CreateBridgeHandoffReplyIfActive` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, INSERT, idempotent constraint branch | none |\n| 3 | `bridge.go:500` | `CreateBridgeHandoffReplyAndOutboxIfActive` | `FOR UPDATE`, INSERT reply, INSERT outbox | none |\n| 4 | `bridge.go:726` | `ClaimPendingBridgeReplyOutbox` | batch claim UPDATEs on status/expiry conditions | none |\n| 5 | `bridge.go:818` | `CompleteClaimedBridgeReplyOutbox` | SELECT, UPDATE, idempotent branch | none |\n| 6 | `bridge.go:912` | `FailClaimedBridgeReplyOutbox` | SELECT, UPDATE, idempotent branch | none |\n| 7 | `bridge.go:1003` | `ClaimBridgeReplyOutboxByOutboxID` | SELECT, claim UPDATE | none |\n| 8 | `agent.go:772` | `CreateAgentMessages` | batch INSERT loop | none |\n\nPlus **non-transactional**: `agent.go:2773-2781` `ClaimPendingEvents` — single `UPDATE … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED … RETURNING` statement (REPOSITORY FACT). Single statements execute in implicit transactions that CockroachDB retries automatically; no wrapper needed (INFERENCE, DOCUMENTATION FACT MCP query 1/7).\n\n### 9.2 Side-effect audit (review Issue 6) — result\nAll 8 transaction bodies are **pure DB operations**: only `QueryRowContext`/`QueryContext`/`ExecContext` against the transaction handle, plus in-memory struct assembly and `uuid.NewString()` for new IDs. External effects (websocket delivery, outbox worker processing, HTTP responses) occur **after** `Commit()` in callers — e.g., `ClaimPendingBridgeReplyOutbox` returns the claimed items and callers deliver them. `uuid.NewString()` regenerates harmlessly on retry (a new unique ID is fine; it is never visible outside the tx result). Conclusion: converting each site to a retry closure introduces **no duplicate side effects**. This audit is recorded as verified, and a code-review check (\"no I/O inside tx closures\") is added to the acceptance criteria (§18).\n\n### 9.3 Wrapper mechanics (cockroach-only)\n- Each of the 8 sites converts to a closure `func(tx *sql.Tx) error` run via `crdb.ExecuteTx(ctx, d.db, nil, fn)` (API at module cache `crdb/tx.go:299`, v2.4.3).\n- `crdb.ExecuteTx` detects SQLSTATE 40001/40003/08xxx retryable errors and re-runs the closure with backoff (DOCUMENTATION FACT: transaction-retry pattern in the pgx tutorial, MCP query 4; repository precedent `vectordb_cockroach.go:191`).\n- Non-retryable errors propagate unchanged to callers; the existing `store.ErrBridge*` sentinel logic is untouched.\n- The string-matching `isPostgresRetryable` loop at `bridge.go:95-104` remains for Postgres; the Cockroach path simply doesn't reach it (the closure retry replaces it).\n- `RunResiliently` (`store/db/postgres/resilience.go`, maxRetries 5, backoff 1s, transient codes 57P01/08006/08003/08001/08004, 23505-as-success) has zero callers today (REPOSITORY FACT). **Not activated** in this plan — the lead's Q5 decision was the 40001 wrapper only; wiring `RunResiliently` is future work (§16).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Experiments (VERIFY-FIRST gates, must run before implementation)\n\n| ID | Question | Method | Pass criterion |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| P1 | Does `SET serial_normalization='sql_sequence'` produce `nextval(...)` defaults through the whole-file path? | Run `LATEST.sql` (prefixed with SET) on single-node Docker via `crdb sql` / app migrator; `SHOW CREATE TABLE` | Defaults show `nextval('…_seq')`, not `unique_rowid()` |\n| P2 | Does whole-file multi-statement exec (no `Begin`) migrate cleanly on Cockroach, and is a failed re-run idempotent? | Execute the full Cockroach `LATEST.sql`; delete `migration_history` row; re-run; also inject a failing statement mid-file and verify history-not-written + successful re-run | Migration succeeds; re-run is no-op via `IF NOT EXISTS`; failed run leaves no history |\n| P3 | Is `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT` accepted as a column default and correct? | `CREATE TABLE t (created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())::BIGINT); INSERT INTO t DEFAULT VALUES; SELECT created_ts;` | Inserts succeed; value equals unix epoch seconds |\n| P4 | Does `crdb.ExecuteTx` retry correctly under contention? | Run `ClaimPendingBridgeReplyOutbox`-style claim from two concurrent connections against the same outbox rows; force a 40001 by conflicting writes | Exactly one claimer wins per row; no duplicated rows; 40001 observed in logs and retried |\n| P5 | SKIP LOCKED claim still correct after port | Run `ClaimPendingEvents` (`agent.go:2781` query) with multiple concurrent workers on Cockroach | Each event claimed exactly once; no double-processing (guards existing behavior, not a new feature) |\n| P6 | Vector path unaffected | Existing `crdb:test` suite (`TestProcessPendingTickets` et al., Taskfile line ~325) | All green with `VECTOR_DB_PROVIDER=cockroach` |\n\n---\n\n## 13. Adversarial pass — every behavioral change defended (review's final prompt)\n\nFor each deviation from the PostgreSQL implementation: (1) exact PG behavior changed, (2) why Cockroach requires it, not merely convenient, (3) new failure modes/regressions.\n\n### 13.1 Migrations: explicit-transaction → autocommit whole-file\n1. **Changed:** a migration file is no longer atomic; statement N failure leaves 1..N-1 applied.\n2. **Required:** Cockroach online schema changes do not support multi-statement DDL transactions; `autocommit_before_ddl` would dissolve the tx anyway (MCP query 6). Keeping `Begin()` would be cosmetic and misleading.\n3. **New failure modes:** partial application on failure. Mitigated by idempotent DDL (`IF NOT EXISTS`), duplicate-tolerance in `execute()` (`migrator.go:326-330`), and history-after-success (§7.3). Residual risk: a *non-idempotent* future migration could fail on re-run — mitigated by requiring all Cockroach migrations to be idempotent (rule added to §18 acceptance criteria) and validated by P2.\n\n### 13.2 Migrations: injected `SET serial_normalization`\n1. **Changed:** none on Postgres (injection is cockroach-only, inside the migrator branch).\n2. **Required:** `int32` IDs overflow with `unique_rowid()` (D2 evidence chain). Without this, every INSERT on Cockroach eventually fails with an out-of-range int32 scan error.\n3. **New failure modes:** none beyond the file itself: the SET is a session variable on the executing connection only; it cannot leak into other pools or sessions. Risk that it silently doesn't apply → P1 gates this.\n4. Regression risk: `sql_sequence` mode performs one `nextval` round-trip per insert (vs. client-generated rowid). For bchat's write volumes (chat messages, agent events) this is negligible (INFERENCE); if it ever matters, `sql_sequence_cached` is the documented alternative (MCP query 2).\n\n### 13.3 DDL: explicit `::BIGINT` casts on EXTRACT defaults\n1. **Changed:** Cockroach files differ textually from Postgres files (19 defaults). Postgres: `numeric → bigint` via assignment cast (rounds); Cockroach: explicit `float → int8` cast (truncates). Both yield whole-second epoch values; a ≤1s difference is theoretically possible at .5s fractional boundaries.\n2. **Required:** `extract(...) → float` in Cockroach and no implicit float→int8 assignment (MCP query 3); without the cast the DDL fails at CREATE TABLE time.\n3. **New failure modes:** none beyond the DDL validation itself, gated by P3. The runtime query `migration_history.go:39` needs no change because it relies on the column default, which the Cockroach DDL now defines correctly.\n\n### 13.4 Runtime: retry closures on 8 tx sites\n1. **Changed:** transaction code becomes a closure; a 40001 causes re-execution instead of error propagation.\n2. **Required:** Cockroach documentation requires client-side retry handling for 40001 (MCP query 9); without it, transient conflicts surface as user-visible failures on a multi-instance Fly.io deployment (INFERENCE).\n3. **New failure modes:** duplicate side effects on retry — audit in §9.2 found none inside closures. ID generation (`uuid.NewString()`) inside closures is safe. The only behavioral nuance: a retried closure may observe newer data on the second attempt — acceptable for these functions (all are either claim/idempotent-by-design or append-only inserts; INFERENCE).\n\n### 13.5 Driver selection/config\n1. **Changed:** a new driver name (`cockroach`) and DSN source (`COCKROACH_DSN`). No behavior change to Postgres/SQLite paths.\n2. **Required:** distinct DSN prevents cross-wiring mistakes in production (D7 rationale).\n3. **New failure modes:** misconfiguration (driver=cockroach without DSN) → fail-fast startup error.\n\n### 13.6 Protocol: simple everywhere\n1. **Changed:** none vs. current Postgres driver (already `simple_protocol`).\n2. **Required:** no — this is the conservative choice; the review's split-protocol idea is optional performance work, not a compatibility requirement. Kept as-is for parity; deferred split documented (§16).\n\n### 13.7 Runtime-created vector schema\n1. **Changed:** none — behavior identical to today's `vectordb_cockroach.go`.\n2. **Required:** no — kept, with the review's requested justification: the schema exists only when the VECTOR capability is compiled in (`cockroach` build tag), making runtime creation the correct boundary.\n\n---\n\n## 14. Risks & known limitations\n\n| Risk | Detail | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|\n| SKIP LOCKED upstream bug #167582 | Under rare conditions, SKIP LOCKED may skip rows whose lock is a stale intent from a committed transaction (GitHub issue surfaced via MCP query 1). Affects `ClaimPendingEvents` claim completeness, not correctness of claiming | Monitor; claims are re-scanned each poll cycle so skipped rows are picked up on the next pass (INFERENCE from poller design). No code change now |\n| 0A000 \"cached plan must not change result type\" | Prepared statements can break across online schema changes | Runtime uses simple protocol (no server-side prepared statements in this path); avoid `SELECT *` (MCP query 12) |\n| Migration atomicity | Files apply statement-by-statement | §7.3 mitigations; idempotency rule; P2 gate |\n| int32 ID space | `sql_sequence` keeps values in int32 range but the space is 2.1B per table | Acceptable for bchat scale (INFERENCE); note in docs; `BIGSERIAL` upgrade is a future decision, not part of this port |\n| EXTRACT float→int truncation | ≤1s deviation possible at .5s boundaries vs. Postgres rounding | Deterministic explicit cast; no business logic depends on sub-second precision (REPOSITORY FACT: all `created_ts`/`updated_ts` consumers read Unix seconds) |\n| Vector index limitations | No `IMPORT INTO` on vector-indexed tables; large batch inserts degrade | Existing provider avoids IMPORT; inserts are single-row UPSERTs (`vectordb_cockroach.go:191`) |\n| Pool sizing | 10 open connections × 2 pools vs. ~4×vCPU guidance | Configurable; verify against actual cluster size at deploy (prod_checklist.md) |\n| simple_protocol performance | Text results, no binary protocol | Accepted; benchmark gate for the split (§16) |\n\n---\n\n## 16. # Docs > Stable
## ALTER TYPE

The `ALTER TYPE` [statement](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/sql-statements) modifies a [user-defined data type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/create-type) in the current database.

Note:
The `ALTER TYPE` statement performs a schema change. For more information about how online schema changes work in CockroachDB, see [Online Schema Changes](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/online-schema-changes).

### Synopsis

ALTER

TYPEtype_name

ADD

VALUE

IF

NOT

EXISTS

value

BEFORE

AFTER

DROP

VALUE

value

RENAME

VALUE

value

TO

value

TOname

SET

SCHEMAschema_name

OWNER

TOrole_spec

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `type_name` | The name of the user-defined type. |
| `ADD VALUE value` | Add a constant value to the user-defined type's list of values. You can optionally specify `BEFORE value` or `AFTER value` to add the value in sort order relative to an existing value. |
| `DROP VALUE value` | Drop a specific value from the user-defined type's list of values. |
| `RENAME TO name` | Rename the user-defined type. |
| `RENAME VALUE value TO value` | Rename a constant value in the user-defined type's list of values. |
| `SET SCHEMA` | Set [the schema](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/sql-name-resolution) of the user-defined type. |
| `OWNER TO` | Change the [role specification](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/grant) for the user-defined type's owner. |

### Required privileges

- To [alter a type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/alter-type), the user must be the owner of the type.
- To set the schema of a user-defined type, the user must have the `CREATE` [privilege](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/security-reference/authorization#managing-privileges) on the schema and the `DROP` privilege
  on the type.
- To alter the owner of a user-defined type:
  - The user executing the command must be a member of the new owner role.
  - The new owner role must have the `CREATE` privilege on the schema the type belongs to.

### Known limitations

- When running the [`ALTER TYPE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/alter-type) statement, you can only reference a user-defined type from the database that contains the type.
- You can only [cancel](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cancel-job) `ALTER TYPE` [schema change jobs](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/online-schema-changes) that drop values. This is because when you drop a value, CockroachDB searches through every row that could contain the type's value, which could take a long time. All other `ALTER TYPE` schema change jobs are [non-cancellable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/cancel-job#known-limitations).

The `ALTER TYPE` statement performs a schema change. For more information about how online schema changes work in CockroachDB, see [Online Schema Changes](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/online-schema-changes).

You can only [cancel](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/cancel-job) `ALTER TYPE` [schema change jobs](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/online-schema-changes) that drop values. This is because when you drop a value, CockroachDB searches through every row that could contain the type's value, which could take a long time.

All other `ALTER TYPE` schema change jobs are non-cancellable.

| Parameter | Description |

| `DROP VALUE value` | Drop a specific value from the user-defined type's list of values. |

- To [alter a type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/alter-type), the user must be the owner of the type.
- To set the schema of a user-defined type, the user must have the `CREATE` [privilege](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v23.2/security-reference/authorization#managing-privileges) on the schema and the `DROP` privilege
  on the type.
- To alter the owner of a user-defined type:

### Known limitations

| `ADD VALUE value` | Add a constant value to the user-defined type's list of values. You can optionally specify `BEFORE value` or `AFTER value` to add the value in sort order relative to an existing value. |
| `DROP VALUE value` | Drop a specific value from the user-defined type's list of values. |
| `RENAME TO name` | Rename the user-defined type. |
| `RENAME VALUE value TO value` | Rename a constant value in the user-defined type's list of values. |
| `SET SCHEMA` | Set [the schema](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/sql-name-resolution) of the user-defined type. |
| `OWNER TO` | Change the [role specification](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/grant) for the user-defined type's owner. |

### Required privileges

- To [alter a type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/alter-type), the user must be the owner of the type.
- To set the schema of a user-defined type, the user must have the `CREATE` [privilege](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/security-reference/authorization#managing-privileges) on the schema and the `DROP` privilege
  on the type.
- To alter the owner of a user-defined type:
  - The user executing the command must be a member of the new owner role.
  - The new owner role must have the `CREATE` privilege on the schema the type belongs to.

### Known limitations

- When running the [`ALTER TYPE`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/alter-type) statement, you can only reference a user-defined type from the database that contains the type.
- You can only [cancel](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/cancel-job) `ALTER TYPE` [schema change jobs](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/online-schema-changes) that drop values. This is because when you drop a value, CockroachDB searches through every row that could contain the type's value, which could take a long time. All other `ALTER TYPE` schema change jobs are [non-cancellable](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.3/cancel-job#known-limitations).

# Github Issue (open): Rust sqlx v0.8.6 Test Failures Against CockroachDB v25.4.3
## Original post

---

**6. Unsupported Built-in Functions (2 failures)**

**Describe the problem**

CockroachDB does not implement `pg_notify()` or `pg_advisory_lock()`.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
SELECT pg_notify(&#x27;chan&#x27;, &#x27;payload&#x27;);
-- ERROR: unknown function: pg_notify()

SELECT pg_advisory_lock(1);
-- ERROR: unknown function: pg_advisory_lock()
```

**Expected behavior**

These are known unsupported functions. Tests should be on the blocklist.

**Additional data**
| Test | Missing Function |
|------|-----------------|
| `it_can_select_void` | `pg_notify()` |
| `test_advisory_locks` | `pg_advisory_lock()` |

---

**7. Constraint Violation Error Classification Differences (3 failures)**

**Describe the problem**

CockroachDB returns error codes that sqlx&#x27;s `ErrorKind` mapping resolves to
`Other` instead of the specific PostgreSQL constraint violation kinds
(`NotNullViolation`, `ForeignKeyViolation`, `CheckViolation`). The tests
create tables inline and trigger constraint violations, but the error code or
structure returned by CockroachDB does not match what sqlx expects from
PostgreSQL.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
CREATE TABLE test_fk_parent (id INT PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE TABLE test_fk_child (id INT PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INT REFERENCES test_fk_parent(id));
INSERT INTO test_fk_child VALUES (1, 999);
-- CockroachDB returns this error, but sqlx classifies it as ErrorKind::Other
-- instead of ErrorKind::ForeignKeyViolation
```

**Expected behavior**

CockroachDB should return PostgreSQL-compatible error codes (SQLSTATE) for
constraint violations so that client libraries can correctly classify them:
- `23502` for NOT NULL violations
- `23503` for foreign key violations
- `23514` for check constraint violations

**Additional data**

| Test | Expected Kind | Got |
|------|---------------|-----|
| `it_fails_with_not_null_violation` | `NotNullViolation` | `Other` |
| `it_fails_with_foreign_key_violation` | `ForeignKeyViolation` | `Other` |
| `it_fails_with_check_violation` | `CheckViolation` | `Other` |

---

**8. DEFERRABLE Constraints Not Supported (1 failure)**

**Describe the problem**

CockroachDB does not support `DEFERRABLE` constraint syntax.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
CREATE TABLE test_defer (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
);
-- ERROR: at or near &quot;deferrable&quot;: syntax error
```

**Expected behavior**

This is a known unsupported feature. The test should be on the blocklist.

**Additional data**

| Test | Error |
|------|-------|
| `test_error_handling_with_deferred_constraints` | `at or near &quot;deferrable&quot;: syntax error` |

---

**9. Domain Types / PL/pgSQL Not Supported (1 failure)**

**Describe the problem**

The test uses a PL/pgSQL `DO $$ ... $$` block with `IF NOT EXISTS` logic to
create domain types within composite types, which CockroachDB does not support.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_type WHERE typname = &#x27;my_domain&#x27;) THEN
    CREATE DOMAIN my_domain AS TEXT;
  END IF;
END $$;
-- ERROR: at or near &quot;if&quot;: syntax error: unimplemented: this syntax
```

**Expected behavior**

This is a known limitation of CockroachDB&#x27;s PL/pgSQL support.

**Additional data**

| Test | Error |
|------|-------|
| `it_supports_domain_types_in_composite_domain_types` | `at or near &quot;if&quot;: syntax error: unimplemented` |

---

**10. Other Behavioral Differences (4 failures)**

**Describe the problem**

Several tests fail due to subtle behavioral differences between CockroachDB and
PostgreSQL in error reporting, prepared statement lifecycle management, error
message content, and floating-point handling.

**Additional data**

**4. CIDR IS NOT DISTINCT FROM Not Supported (4 failures)**

# Github Issue (open): Rust sqlx v0.8.6 Test Failures Against CockroachDB v25.4.3
## Original post

**Describe the problem**

Running the Rust [sqlx](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx) v0.8.6 integration
test suite against CockroachDB v25.4.3 results in 59 test failures and 2
cargo-ignored tests out of 208 total (147 pass). The failures fall into several
categories of PostgreSQL compatibility gaps.

**To Reproduce**

1. Start a single-node CockroachDB v25.4.3 cluster in insecure mode.
2. Create a database and user for the tests:
   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS sqlx;
   CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS postgres WITH CREATEDB CREATELOGIN CREATEROLE CANCELQUERY;
   GRANT ALL ON DATABASE sqlx TO postgres;
   SET CLUSTER SETTING sql.defaults.default_int_size = 4;
   ```
3. Clone sqlx v0.8.6:
   ```bash
   git clone --branch v0.8.6 https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx.git /tmp/sqlx
   ```
4. Run the postgres integration tests:
   ```bash
   cd /tmp/sqlx &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=&#x27;postgresql://postgres@localhost:26257/sqlx?sslmode=disable&#x27; \
     cargo test \
       --features postgres,runtime-tokio,tls-none,_unstable-all-types \
       --test postgres \
       --test postgres-types \
       --test postgres-describe \
       --test postgres-error \
       --test postgres-query-builder \
       --no-fail-fast
   ```
5. Observe 59 failures across 4 of the 5 test targets (`postgres-query-builder`
   passes entirely).

**Expected behavior**

All tests that exercise standard SQL and PostgreSQL wire-protocol features
supported by CockroachDB should pass. Tests that use genuinely unsupported
PostgreSQL extensions (LISTEN/NOTIFY, advisory locks, MACADDR, MONEY, etc.)
are expected to fail and belong on the blocklist.

**Environment:**
- CockroachDB version: v25.4.3
- Server OS: macOS Darwin 25.3.0 (arm64); also reproducible on Linux
- Client app: Rust sqlx v0.8.6 via `cargo test`

---

**Failure Categories**

**1. INT Type Mismatch (19 failures)**

**Describe the problem**

CockroachDB returns `INT8` (OID 20) for integer literal expressions like
`SELECT 1 + 1` even when `sql.defaults.default_int_size = 4` is set. That
cluster setting only affects the default column type in `CREATE TABLE`
statements, not the inferred type of integer literals and arithmetic
expressions in queries.

sqlx strictly checks the wire-protocol type OID when decoding results. When a
Rust `i32` is expected (mapped to PostgreSQL `INT4`, OID 23), but CockroachDB
returns `INT8` (OID 20), sqlx rejects the value with a `ColumnDecode` error.

**To Reproduce**

```sql
-- CockroachDB returns INT8 for this expression even with default_int_size = 4
SELECT pg_typeof(1 + 1);  -- returns &#x27;bigint&#x27; (INT8)
```

```
Error: mismatched types; Rust type `i32` (as SQL type `INT4`) is not compatible with SQL type `INT8`
```

**Expected behavior**

Integer literal expressions should return `INT4` (OID 23) when
`sql.defaults.default_int_size = 4`, matching PostgreSQL&#x27;s behavior where
`SELECT 1 + 1` returns `integer` (INT4).

**Additional data**

# Blog > Durable Execution with DBOS and CockroachDB
## **How to deploy DBOS on CockroachDB**

There are two required configuration changes when using CockroachDB instead of PostgreSQL.

#### **Prerequisites**

pip install "dbos[otel]==2.15.0" "fastapi[standard]" psycopg2-binary sqlalchemy-cockroachdb``export DBOS_COCKROACHDB_URL="postgresql://<user>:<password>@<crdb-host>:26257/dbos_system?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/certs/ca.crt" ```### [1. **Disable** `**LISTEN/NOTIFY**`](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/embedded-durable-execution-dbos-cockroachdb/#1.-Disable-LISTEN/NOTIFY)

PostgreSQL’s `LISTEN/NOTIFY` mechanism is used by DBOS to wake up waiting workflows without polling. CockroachDB does not implement this mechanism, so it must be disabled explicitly; DBOS falls back to polling automatically:

Show code ### [**2. Set the system database URL**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/embedded-durable-execution-dbos-cockroachdb/#2.-Set-the-system-database-URL)

In `dbos-config.yaml`, point the system database at CockroachDB using the standard PostgreSQL connection string format:

`name: my-agent-app language: python runtimeConfig:   start:     - python3 app/main.py system_database_url: ${DBOS_COCKROACHDB_URL}`Set the environment variable with your CockroachDB connection string:

`export DBOS_COCKROACHDB_URL="postgresql://dbos_user:password@<crdb-host>:26257/dbos_system?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/certs/ca.crt"`## [**Build a durable AI agent workflow with DBOS and CockroachDB**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/embedded-durable-execution-dbos-cockroachdb/#Build-a-durable-AI-agent-workflow-with-DBOS-and-CockroachDB)

The following example implements a three-step durable agent workflow backed by CockroachDB. The workflow publishes progress events after each step that a frontend can poll in real time. If the process crashes mid-execution, restarting it resumes from the last completed step: no re-billing, no duplicate writes, no lost context.

Show code Install dependencies and run:

`pip install "dbos[otel]==2.15.0" "fastapi[standard]" psycopg2-binary sqlalchemy-cockroachdb export DBOS_COCKROACHDB_URL="postgresql://dbos_user:pass@localhost:26257/dbos_system?sslmode=disable" python3 app/main.py`## [**Benchmarking**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/embedded-durable-execution-dbos-cockroachdb/#Benchmarking)

Durable execution introduces additional coordination because workflow progress must be safely recorded after every completed step. The important architectural question isn’t simply how quickly a database can write rows, but whether it can continue supporting growing numbers of durable workflows while preserving correctness, availability, and operational simplicity. The following benchmarks compare PostgreSQL and CockroachDB under identical conditions to measure both raw database throughput and end-to-end DBOS workflow execution.

### [**Test environment**](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/embedded-durable-execution-dbos-cockroachdb/#Test-environment)

All benchmarks ran from an EC2 instance co-located in AWS **us-east-1**, eliminating WAN overhead:

- **PostgreSQL RDS 17**: `db.m7i.24xlarge`, 96 vCPU, 384 GB RAM, gp3 500 GiB, 16,000 IOPS, 1,000 MB/s throughput
- **CockroachDB 3 nodes**: `3× m7i.8xlarge`, 96 vCPU total, nodes spread across **multiple us-east-1 AZs** (genuine zone-redundant deployment)

# Docs > V25.3 > Troubleshoot SQL Statements
## Unsupported SQL features

CockroachDB has support for [most SQL features](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/sql-feature-support).

Additionally, CockroachDB supports [the PostgreSQL wire protocol and the majority of its syntax](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/postgresql-compatibility). This means that existing applications can often be migrated to CockroachDB without changing application code.

However, you may encounter features of SQL or the PostgreSQL dialect that are not supported by CockroachDB. For example, the following PostgreSQL features are not supported:

- Events.
- Drop primary key.

Note:
Each table must have a primary key associated with it. You can [drop and add a primary key constraint within a single transaction](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/alter-table#drop-and-add-a-primary-key-constraint).

- XML functions.
- Column-level privileges.
- XA syntax.
- Creating a database from a template.
- [Dropping a single partition from a table](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/partitioning#known-limitations).
- Foreign data wrappers.
- Advisory Lock Functions (although some functions are defined with no-op implementations).

For more information about the differences between CockroachDB and PostgreSQL feature support, see [PostgreSQL Compatibility](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/postgresql-compatibility).

For more information about the SQL standard features supported by CockroachDB, see [SQL Feature Support](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v25.3/sql-feature-support).

# Docs > V24.2 > Troubleshoot SQL Statements
## Unsupported SQL features

CockroachDB has support for [most SQL features](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/sql-feature-support).

Additionally, CockroachDB supports [the PostgreSQL wire protocol and the majority of its syntax](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/postgresql-compatibility). This means that existing applications can often be migrated to CockroachDB without changing application code.

However, you may encounter features of SQL or the PostgreSQL dialect that are not supported by CockroachDB. For example, the following PostgreSQL features are not supported:

- Triggers. These must be implemented in your application logic.
- Events.
- Drop primary key.

Note:
Each table must have a primary key associated with it. You can [drop and add a primary key constraint within a single transaction](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/alter-table#drop-and-add-a-primary-key-constraint).

- XML functions.
- Column-level privileges.
- XA syntax.
- Creating a database from a template.
- [Dropping a single partition from a table](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/partitioning#known-limitations).
- Foreign data wrappers.
- Advisory Lock Functions (although some functions are defined with no-op implementations).

For more information about the differences between CockroachDB and PostgreSQL feature support, see [PostgreSQL Compatibility](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/postgresql-compatibility).

For more information about the SQL standard features supported by CockroachDB, see [SQL Feature Support](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/sql-feature-support).

1. createBridgeHandoffAttempt (bridge.go:112): generation = MAX+1 computed in-tx; on retry recomputed → **may observe newer state; optimistic by design** (generation monotonic guard; conflict errors preserved).
2. CreateBridgeHandoffReplyIfActive (356): FOR UPDATE + guarded INSERT; retry re-reads handoff → **may observe newer state; guards preserve conflict semantics**.
3. CreateBridgeHandoffReplyAndOutboxIfActive (500): same → **may observe newer state; guards preserve conflict semantics**.
4. ClaimPendingBridgeReplyOutbox (726): claim via guarded UPDATEs (WHERE status/expiry); failed attempt's writes rolled back; retry sees fewer candidates → **may observe newer state; claim guards make it safe**.
5. CompleteClaimedBridgeReplyOutbox (818): claim_token-guarded UPDATE + idempotent completion branch → **deterministic under retry**.
6. FailClaimedBridgeReplyOutbox (912): same → **deterministic under retry**.
7. ClaimBridgeReplyOutboxByOutboxID (1003): guarded claim UPDATE → **may observe newer state; guard-safe**.
8. CreateAgentMessages (agent.go:772): append-only INSERTs; retry re-inserts from scratch (failed attempt rolled back) → **deterministic under retry**.
Plus ClaimPendingEvents single-statement: server-retried; SKIP LOCKED → deterministic per claim (each event claimed once).

Key mechanical fact to state: 40001 abort rolls back the failed attempt's writes, so retries never double-write; the only variability is reads observing newer committed state, which every site tolerates via guards (WHERE claim conditions, claim_token) or by design (MAX+1, append).

One more MCP check: UPDATE ... FROM support. Let me search. Also verify "INSERT INTO tenant_role_templates" statement has ON CONFLICT.

Strong findings: **LISTEN/NOTIFY unsupported**, **advisory locks unsupported (no-op stubs)**, **CREATE DOMAIN unsupported**, **range types/MACADDR/MONEY unsupported**, **triggers unsupported**, **DEFERRABLE unsupported**, **drop-primary-key unsupported** — but **ALTER TYPE is supported** (v23.1+). # Docs > Stable > UPDATE
## Reference other tables in an update

To reference values from a table other than the table being updated, add a `FROM` clause that specifies one or more tables in the cluster. Values from tables specified in a `FROM` clause can be used in `UPDATE` expressions, and in `RETURNING` and `WHERE` clauses.

When executing an `UPDATE` query with a `FROM` clause, CockroachDB [joins](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/joins) the target table (i.e., the table being updated) to the tables referenced in the `FROM` clause. The output of this join should have the same number of rows as the rows being updated in the target table, as CockroachDB uses a single row from the join output to update a given row in the target table. If the join produces more rows than the rows being updated in the target table, there is no way to predict which row from the join output will be used to update a row in the target table.

For an example, see [Update using values from a different table](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/update#update-using-values-from-a-different-table).

# Docs > Stable
## UPDATE

The `UPDATE` [statement](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/sql-statements) updates rows in a table.

Warning:
If you update a row that contains a column referenced by a [foreign key constraint](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/foreign-key) and has an [`ON UPDATE` action](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/foreign-key#foreign-key-actions), all of the dependent rows will also be updated.

### Required privileges

The user must have the `SELECT` and `UPDATE` [privileges](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/security-reference/authorization#managing-privileges) on the table.

### Synopsis

WITH

RECURSIVEcommon_table_expr

,

UPDATE

ONLYtable_nameopt_index_flags

-

AStable_alias_name

SETcolumn_name

=a_expr

(column_name

,

)

\=

(select_stmta_expr

,a_expr

,

)

,

FROMtable_ref

,

WHEREa_exprsort_clauselimit_clause

RETURNINGtarget_list

NOTHING

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `common_table_expr` | See [Common Table Expressions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/common-table-expressions). |
| `table_name` | The name of the table that contains the rows you want to update. |
| `AS table_alias_name` | An alias for the table name. When an alias is provided, it completely hides the actual table name. |
| `column_name` | The name of the column whose values you want to update. |
| `a_expr` | The new value you want to use, the [aggregate function](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/functions-and-operators#aggregate-functions) you want to perform, or the [scalar expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/scalar-expressions) you want to use.To fill columns with their [default values](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/default-value), use `DEFAULT VALUES` in place of `a_expr`. To fill a specific column with its default value, leave the value out of the `a_expr` or use `DEFAULT` at the appropriate position. |
| `FROM table_ref` | Specify a table to reference, but not update, in `UPDATE` expressions, or in `RETURNING` and `WHERE` clauses. For more details, see [Reference other tables in an update](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/update#reference-other-tables-in-an-update). |
| `select_stmt` | A [selection query](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/selection-queries). Each value must match the [data type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/data-types) of its column on the left side of `=`. |
| `WHERE a_expr` | `a_expr` must be a [scalar expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/scalar-expressions) that returns Boolean values using columns (e.g., `<column> = <value>`). Update rows that return `TRUE`.**Without a `WHERE` clause in your statement, `UPDATE` updates all rows in the table.** |
| `sort_clause` | An `ORDER BY` clause. See [Ordering Query Results](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/order-by) and [Ordering of rows in DML statements](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/order-by#ordering-rows-in-dml-statements) for more details. |
| `limit_clause` | A `LIMIT` clause. See [Limit Query Results](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/limit-offset) for more details. |
| `RETURNING target_list` | Return values based on rows updated, where `target_list` can be specific column names from the table, `*` for all columns, or computations using [scalar expressions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.2/scalar-expressions). To return nothing in the response, not even the number of rows updated, use `RETURNING NOTHING`. |
| `ONLY ... *` | Supported for compatibility with PostgreSQL table inheritance syntax. This clause is a no-op, as CockroachDB does not currently support table inheritance. |

| `table_name` | The name of the table that contains the rows you want to update. |
| `AS table_alias_name` | An alias for the table name. When an alias is provided, it completely hides the actual table name. |
| `column_name` | The name of the column whose values you want to update. |
| `a_expr` | The new value you want to use, the [aggregate function](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/functions-and-operators#aggregate-functions) you want to perform, or the [scalar expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/scalar-expressions) you want to use.To fill columns with their [default values](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/default-value), use `DEFAULT VALUES` in place of `a_expr`. To fill a specific column with its default value, leave the value out of the `a_expr` or use `DEFAULT` at the appropriate position. |
| `FROM table_ref` | Specify a table to reference, but not update, in `UPDATE` expressions, or in `RETURNING` and `WHERE` clauses. For more details, see [Reference other tables in an update](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/update#reference-other-tables-in-an-update). |
| `select_stmt` | A [selection query](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/selection-queries). Each value must match the [data type](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/data-types) of its column on the left side of `=`. |
| `WHERE a_expr` | `a_expr` must be a [scalar expression](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/scalar-expressions) that returns Boolean values using columns (e.g., `<column> = <value>`). Update rows that return `TRUE`.**Without a `WHERE` clause in your statement, `UPDATE` updates all rows in the table.** |
| `sort_clause` | An `ORDER BY` clause. See [Ordering Query Results](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/order-by) and [Ordering of rows in DML statements](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/order-by#ordering-rows-in-dml-statements) for more details. |
| `limit_clause` | A `LIMIT` clause. See [Limit Query Results](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/limit-offset) for more details. |
| `RETURNING target_list` | Return values based on rows updated, where `target_list` can be specific column names from the table, `*` for all columns, or computations using [scalar expressions](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v26.1/scalar-expressions). To return nothing in the response, not even the number of rows updated, use `RETURNING NOTHING`. |
| `ONLY ... *` | Supported for compatibility with PostgreSQL table inheritance syntax. This clause is a no-op, as CockroachDB does not currently support table inheritance. |
```
